info.title: Insolvia API
info.description: The API the Insolvia app calls (`backend/src/Insolvia.Api`). Generated by `tool/render-openapi.ts` from `tool/openapi/api-routes.ts` and the API client's types — do not edit by hand. Errors share one envelope: `{"error": <code>, "message": <text>}`, or `{"error": "ValidationError", "fields": {<field>: <message>}}` for a 400 naming fields. A 404 means unknown *or* not yours: the API answers both the same way.

get.summary: The API's liveness/identity endpoint.

Every event the caller may see that overlaps the window: the firm's own events plus those on cases the caller can open. The server applies the case access rule; a `caseId` the caller cannot see answers empty, never 404.
get.description: Requires `events:view_only`.

get.summary: The signed-in caller's cases, paginated.
get.description:
`limit` and `cursor` are both optional and, per this package's rule, omitted from the query string entirely when absent — see `listCasesQuery`. `nextCursor` on the result is absent, not `null`, on the last page.

Requires `cases:view_only`.

post.summary: Start a new case.
post.description:
Protected: same bearer-token mechanism as `me`. Returns the created `Case` on 201. Throws `ApiValidationException` on a 400 with per-field messages (e.g. an out-of-range chapter).

Requires `cases:add_edit` and `clients:view_only`.

get.summary: A single case by id.
get.description:
Throws a plain `ApiException` (statusCode `404`) when `caseId` is unknown **or** belongs to a different caller — the API deliberately answers both the same way, so a 404 here must never be rendered as "this case does not exist" in the UI.

Requires `cases:view_only`.

patch.summary: Change a subset of a case's fields.
patch.description:
`changes` may hold any subset of `UpdateCaseChanges`; omitted keys mean "leave unchanged" and are never sent — see `updateCaseChangesToJson`. Returns the updated `Case` on 200.

Like `getCase`, a 404 means unknown *or* not-owned; see that method's note.

Requires `cases:add_edit`.

delete.summary: Soft-delete a case (issue #355): from then on every read answers 404, and nothing is removed. A FIRM ADMIN's act (403 otherwise), and refused with a 409 on a case that has been filed — archive that instead.

put.summary: Archive the case (`true`) or restore it to the working list (`false`). Idempotent; returns the `Case` with `Case.archivedAt` set or absent. Any status may be archived.

get.summary: Who is linked to this case.
get.description:
Subjects, not names: resolve them through `listFirmDirectory`. Copying a display name onto an assignment would go stale the moment somebody is renamed.

A 404 means the case is unknown, another firm's, *or* one the caller is not linked to — see `getCase`.

Requires `cases:view_only`.

put.summary: Put a colleague on a case.
put.description:
**Idempotent.** Linking somebody already on the matter succeeds, which is why it is a PUT: a client that lost a response can simply repeat it.

Needs `cases: add_edit`, not an administrative permission — putting a colleague on a matter is case work. A 404 covers a case the caller cannot reach *and* a subject who is not in their firm, deliberately: telling them apart would be a probe for who works where.

Requires `cases:add_edit`.

delete.description:
**A caller can unlink themselves and lose the case they were just editing.** That is the honest consequence of "I am no longer on this matter"; a client should confirm before doing it to the signed-in user.

Unlinking the LAST person is allowed — the firm's administrators still reach the case, so it can always be reassigned. 404 when the subject is not on the case.

Requires `cases:add_edit`.

post.summary: Record a conversion of a filed case to another chapter.
post.description:
Filed cases only (409 otherwise). `toChapter` must be a real chapter different from the current one, and `effectiveOn` (`YYYY-MM-DD`) no earlier than the petition or the previous court event (400 naming the field). Answers the case as written and the lifecycle event it recorded.

Requires `cases:add_edit`.

post.summary: Open a NEW case from this one's data (issue #355): its debtors, schedules and petition answers, each value's provenance naming the source in `copied_from_case_id`. Returns the new `Case` (201), opened at `intake`. A 409 means a client the source names is archived or merged, or its Debtor 1 has no client.
post.description: Requires `cases:add_edit` and `clients:view_only`.

get.summary: Generate the court's creditor mailing matrix from the case's creditor records (issue #94).
get.description:
Always a 200: the outcome is either the file (`content` present, `problems` empty) or the reasons there isn't one (`problems` non-empty, `content` absent) — never both, and never a partial file. Like `getCase`, a 404 means the case is unknown *or* not the caller's.

Requires `intake:view_only`.

get.summary: Every debtor of one case, in the order the forms print them (`debtor_1`, `debtor_2`, `non_filing_spouse`).
get.description:
The wire body is `{"debtors": [...]}`; this returns the array. There is no pagination and no second key to carry — a case has at most three debtors — so a result object would be an envelope with one thing in it, unlike `ListCasesResult`, which exists to carry `nextCursor`.

A case with no debtors saved yet is an empty array, not a 404. Like `getCase`, a 404 means the case is unknown *or* not the caller's.

Requires `intake:view_only`.

put.summary: Save one debtor of a case, whole, and get the saved record back.
put.description:
**The whole record, every time.** This replaces rather than merges, so a field left out of `debtor` is cleared. See `PutDebtorRequest` for why the endpoint is a PUT.

Every populated field needs a `provenance` entry or the API answers 400; `staffTypedProvenance` builds that map.

**Accepts 200 and 201, and nothing else in between.** The API answers 201 when the role had no record yet and 200 when it replaced one — the same request either way, since an autosave neither knows nor cares which it is doing. The two are listed explicitly rather than testing `response.ok`, because "any 2xx" would quietly swallow a 202 or a 204 from a proxy that never reached this endpoint, and then fail on the missing body with a message about a malformed debtor.

The distinction is deliberately not returned: nothing in the app branches on it, and the record carries `created_at` and `updated_at` for anything that would.

Like `getCase`, a 404 means the case is unknown *or* not the caller's; see that method's note.

Requires `intake:add_edit`.

put.summary: Link a firm client to one debtor of a case (ADR 0022). The only way a debtor's `client_id` changes after the case is opened: `putDebtor` keeps it.
put.description:
With no debtor in that role yet, the client is COPIED in (201) — how a joint case gains its Debtor 2, since a questionnaire save can no longer create one from nothing. With one already there, only the link moves (200); the case's copied fields stay, and where they now disagree with the client is `Debtor.differs_from_client`.

Needs `intake` at `add_edit` and `clients` at `view_only`. Throws `ApiValidationException` keyed `client_id` for an unknown, foreign or archived client, or one already holding another role on this case.

Requires `intake:add_edit` and `clients:view_only`.

post.summary: ADR 0022's *re-copy from client*: the debtor's copied fields (name, other names, both addresses, phone, mobile, email) are overwritten with the linked client's, each with `client` provenance again, and the saved debtor comes back (its `differs_from_client` now `[]`). The case's own answers — venue, counselling, the signature date, the tax ID — are untouched. No body.
post.description:
Throws a plain `ApiException` with `statusCode` **409** when the case is filed (changing a filed petition is an amendment) or the debtor has no linked client, and `ApiValidationException` keyed `client_id` when that client is archived. Needs `intake` at `add_edit` and `clients` at `view_only`.

Requires `intake:add_edit` and `clients:view_only`.

post.summary: ADR 0022's *update client from this case*: the linked client's copied fields are overwritten with what this debtor now says (the client's own date of birth, lead source and so on are kept). Answers the DEBTOR, unchanged but for `differs_from_client`, now `[]`. No body.
post.description:
Allowed on a filed case — the petition does not change, the directory does. Throws a plain `ApiException` with `statusCode` **409** when the debtor has no linked client, and `ApiValidationException` keyed `name` when the case's name is empty (a client needs one). Needs `clients` at `add_edit`.

Requires `intake:view_only` and `clients:add_edit`.

get.summary: Every request of the case, in the order asked, with arrived-vs-outstanding progress. `documents` at `view_only`.
get.description: Requires `documents:view_only`.

post.summary: Ask for one more document. 201.
post.description: Requires `documents:add_edit`.

post.summary: Request every entry of the firm's checklist the case has not already asked for. Safe to repeat; `added` says how many this call created.
post.description: Requires `documents:add_edit`.

patch.summary: Waive or reopen. `received` is not settable: a completed upload is what receives a request.

get.summary: Every document of one case, newest first.
get.description:
Not paginated (the answer is bounded by one case's paperwork), so this returns the array itself rather than a result object with a cursor.

**Pending documents are included**, and filtering them out here would be a mistake: a row whose upload never finished is the case's own record of a file the user tried to add, and `Document.status` is what lets the UI offer a retry instead of losing it silently.

Requires `documents:view_only`.

post.summary: Record a document and mint a capability to upload its bytes.
post.description:
**This is step one of three, and the record it creates is not a document yet.** It comes back `status: 'pending'`, and a pending record whose `completeDocument` never runs is deleted by the bucket's lifecycle rule 24 hours later. Prefer `uploadDocument`, which runs all three steps; reach for this only when the PUT has to happen somewhere this client cannot see (a background transfer, a native uploader).

Throws `ApiValidationException` on a 400 — per-field messages keyed `kind`, `fileName`, `contentType`, `byteSize`. Throws a plain `ApiException` (404) when the case is unknown *or* not the caller's; see `getCase`.

Requires `documents:add_edit`.

delete.summary: Remove a document from its case and make its bytes unreachable.
delete.description:
Answers **204 with no body**, so this resolves to nothing: there is no record to hand back, and echoing one would invite treating the response as the document.

"Unreachable", not "destroyed": the bucket is versioned, so the object stops resolving immediately while the bytes remain as a noncurrent version for 30 days. That is the answer a caller asking under a retention or erasure obligation needs.

Throws a plain `ApiException` (404) for an unknown document, an unknown case, or a case that is not the caller's — all four the same way.

Requires `documents:add_edit`.

post.summary: Tell the API the PUT finished, and get the confirmed record back.
post.description:
**This is the step that keeps the document.** The server checks the object really is in the bucket, clears the tag the bucket's reaper filters on, and writes the record back as `'stored'` with the size S3 actually counted. Until it runs, the object still carries `upload=unconfirmed` and is deleted 24 hours after it was written.

Idempotent — a client that retries because it lost the response gets the same record.

Throws a plain `ApiException` with `statusCode` **409** when the object is not in the bucket, which means the bytes never arrived: the record stays `'pending'` and the honest next move is to upload again, not to retry this call. `isUploadIncomplete` is that check.

Requires `documents:add_edit`.

get.summary: A short-lived URL that serves one document's bytes.
get.description:
Ask at the moment of use and do not cache: the URL expires in minutes, and it is a bearer capability — anything holding it can read the document, so it does not belong in a log, a query string you control, or persisted state. A fresh one is a single round trip.

A `'pending'` document has a record but no object: the URL mints fine and answers 404 when followed. Check `Document.status` first.

Requires `documents:view_only`.

get.summary: A case's events, hand-made and generated, dismissed included, in start order. Gated by `events` (`view_only`); a 404 means the case is unknown or not the caller's.
get.description: Requires `events:view_only`.

post.summary: Add a hand-made event to a case.
post.description: Requires `events:add_edit`.

get.summary: One event on a case's calendar.
get.description: Requires `events:view_only`.

put.summary: Replace a hand-made event whole. A generated deadline answers 400: change the case's dates instead.

patch.summary: `PATCH /v1/cases/{caseId}/events/{id}` with `{"dismissed"}` — the one edit a generated deadline admits ("filed with the petition"), and it survives regeneration. Works on a hand-made event too.

delete.summary: A hand-made event only; a generated one is 400.

get.summary: The Schedule C workbench's read (issue #346): the statutes this case may claim under given its election and expected filing date, what it has claimed against each, and every asset's value − liens − claimed, all computed server-side.
get.description:
NOT `/exemptions`: that URL is the exemption records' own collection route (`listCaseEntities` with `'exemptions'`), which the panel still uses to add and remove claims. Fetch this beside an asset, and
**never add the figures up in a screen** (ADR 0001).

Always 200 with `problems` for what could not resolve. Like `getCase`, a 404 means the case is unknown *or* not the caller's.

Requires `intake:view_only`.

get.summary: The case's review queue (issue 8.9): machine-proposed records awaiting, or past, human confirmation. Both streams — document extraction and MCP agent proposals — distinguishable only by each row's `origin`.
get.description:
Gated on the `extraction_review` feature: `hidden` answers 403 (check `me.permissions` before routing here), `view_only` and up may read. `status` narrows server-side; the review screen reads `'pending'`.

Requires `extraction_review:view_only`.

post.summary: The one confirmation act (issue 8.9): accept a pending candidate into the case (optionally with the record as the human corrected it), or reject it. Requires `extraction_review: add_edit`; `view_only` gets a 403 here while the listing above still answers.
post.description:
Throws `ApiValidationException` on a 400 — including the "confirm the referenced creditor/employment candidate first" refusal, keyed by the reference field — and a plain `ApiException` with 409 when the candidate was already reviewed (by this reviewer's own earlier call, or by a colleague who won the race).

Requires `extraction_review:add_edit`.

get.summary: What an approval of this case's filing would cover (ADR 0024, guardrail 1: the court, the documents in docket order with sizes and digests, the checklist, the fee handling, and the digest over it all) and the case's current approval. An approval whose filing set has changed since comes back `voided` (`changed`). Needs `electronic_filing` at `view_only`.
get.description: Requires `cases:view_only` and `electronic_filing:view_only`.

post.summary: Approve exactly the filing set the caller was shown, named by its `digest`. Throws `ApiReauthenticationRequiredException` when the sign-in is not recent (sign in again with a forced prompt, then retry); a 409 means the filing set changed since it was shown, has a blocker (`FilingSetNotReady`, with `blockers`), or is already being filed; a 403 that the caller holds no login of their own for this court, or no current authorization. `credentialId` is needed only when the caller has two logins for the court. Needs `electronic_filing` at `add_edit`.
post.description: Requires `cases:view_only` and `electronic_filing:add_edit`.

delete.summary: Cancel the pending approval before the filing worker uses it. A 409 means nothing is pending. Needs `electronic_filing` at `view_only`: stopping a filing only ever takes authority away.

get.summary: The filing set and hand-off checklist for the case's court (ADR 0024 build PR 3): the documents in the court's docket order and upload names, each checked against the court's size, text-layer and page-size rules, and a checklist saying what is ready, what is missing and why, and where in the app to fix it. Files nothing. Like `getCase`, a 404 means the case is unknown *or* not the caller's.
get.description: Requires `cases:view_only`.

post.summary: `POST /v1/cases/{caseId}/filings/{filingId}/resolution` (ADR 0024 PR 8) — record what the court's docket shows for a handed-back or unknown-outcome filing. ALWAYS sends `docket_checked: true`: call it only once the attorney has confirmed they checked the court's own docket. `filed` files the case with the number and petition date given; `not_filed` frees it for a new approval. A 403 means the caller is not the filing's attorney; a 409 (`ResolutionRefused`, with `reason`) that it is already resolved (`not_resolvable`), the court confirmed it (`court_confirmed`), or the attempt may still be live (`attempt_may_be_live`); a 400 names the field. Returns the `FilingApprovalView`, as `getFilingApproval` does.
post.description: Requires `cases:add_edit` and `electronic_filing:add_edit`.

get.summary: The forms hub (issue 13.2 / #343): every form this case's chapter and pin require, each with its item count or dollar total (where the hub defines one) and the completeness problems that belong to it, grouped per form rather than flattened.
get.description:
Built entirely from the same gate `getCaseSummary` and `acceptCaseJob`'s `packet_assembly` kind run — a form listed here with no problems is a form the packet would actually include. Like `getCase`, a 404 means the case is unknown *or* not the caller's.

Requires `cases:view_only`.

get.summary: Render exactly one form through the same fill engine `packet_assembly` uses, and mint a short-lived URL to the PDF.
get.description:
Always 200: the outcome is either the URL (`FormPreview.problems` empty) or every reason the form could not render yet (FormPreview.url absent) — never both, and never a partial form, the creditor-matrix route's own contract applied to one form.

`form` is the SHORT key (`CaseForm.form`, e.g. `'b106ab'`), not the `'form/…'` series id `CaseForm.series` carries. A form this case does not currently file (an unknown key, or one `listCaseForms` is not showing right now — B106J-2 with no separate household, B122A-2 below the median) is a 404: the same not-part-of-this-case reading a foreign packet id gets.

`options` (issue 13.11) is the query-string spelling of the same output options `acceptCaseJob`'s `outputOptions` carries, minus `forms` — this route already names one form — via `formPreviewQuery`. Omitted entirely renders the plain bytes, exactly as before this option existed.

Requires `cases:view_only`.

post.summary: Hand minutes-long work to the async pipeline (ADR 0018). Body is `{"kind"}` and nothing else: workers read everything from the case, so there is no payload to send.
post.description:
Always 202 with the `Job` now in flight — which is a FRESH job, or the already-active one of the same kind: one active job per (case, kind) is the server's idempotency rule, so re-calling this after a timeout is safe and never starts a duplicate run. Poll `getCaseJob` until the status settles.

`outputOptions` (issue 13.11) is the `packet_assembly` kind's own field — a "Draft" watermark, the top-margin date/time, signature-page selection, `/s/` electronic signatures, and a chosen subset of forms. Omitted entirely means the plain filing set, exactly as every packet before this option existed; every other kind refuses it, the `documentId` rule's own shape.

Throws `ApiValidationException` on a 400 (message keyed `kind`, `documentId`, or an `outputOptions` field such as `signaturePages` or an unfiled `forms` entry); a plain `ApiException` with 404 when the case is unknown *or* not the caller's (see `getCase`), and with 503 in the brief deploy window where this environment's pipeline is not up yet — retry later.

Requires `cases:add_edit`.

get.summary: One job's status.
get.description:
Like `getCase`, a 404 means the case is unknown *or* not the caller's — and also covers a job id from another case, which does not resolve here by construction.

Requires `cases:view_only`.

get.summary: What each secured claim is secured by and what each asset carries (issue #345): the claim read path for the derived collateral figures.
get.description:
The generic collection routes never special-case a kind, so a claim's secured and unsecured portions — arithmetic over the claim, its asset and the liens senior to it — do not ride on `getCaseEntity`. They come from here: one light read of the assets and the claims, the same function B106D prints Column B from. Fetch it beside a claim or an asset; **never add the figures up in a screen** (ADR 0001).

The summary carries the same block for the overview, but runs the whole completeness gate to get there; a form under a preparer's cursor should call this. Like `getCase`, a 404 means the case is unknown *or* not the caller's.

Requires `intake:view_only`.

get.summary: The case's lifecycle history, oldest first.
get.description:
Every status change, conversion and confirmation ruling (ADR 0027). `GET …/status-history` is the same history's status events in an older shape.

Requires `cases:view_only`.

get.summary: The § 707(b) trace for the case as of its expected filing date (issue #349): CMI by line and column with the window used, the median comparison, and for an above-median debtor the B122A-2 lines and the presumption result, every figure naming where it came from. Run by the same code path the packet's B122A-1/A-2 use, so the screen and the forms never disagree.
get.description:
Always resolves to 200; read `CaseMeansTest.problems` when `outcome` is `undetermined`. Like `getCaseSummary`, a 404 means the case is unknown *or* not the caller's.

Requires `cases:view_only`.

get.summary: Every note on the case, NEWEST FIRST (the server's own order — the opposite of `listCaseEntities`, which lists a schedule oldest first; a note is a running log, so the one just left belongs at the top). The wire body is `{"notes": [...]}`; this returns the array.
get.description: Requires `notes:view_only`.

post.summary: Add one note (issue 14.5 / #357), case- level or anchored to a form. The server stamps `authorSubject`/ `authorName` from the caller's own token; `NoteRequest` carries neither, so there is nothing to send and nothing to spoof.
post.description:
A STATIC segment, not `addCaseEntity` — `note`s are not a `CaseCollection`; see the module comment above `NoteRequest`.

Requires `notes:add_edit`.

put.summary: Replace a note's text and form anchor, WHOLE, exactly as `putCaseEntity` replaces a collection record. Authorship never changes here, including when a firm admin edits a colleague's note — the server keeps the ORIGINAL author.
put.description:
A 403 means the caller is neither the note's author nor a firm admin — see `ApiException.statusCode` — distinct from the 403 a missing `notes` permission would answer, and from a 404, which this endpoint still uses for a note the caller cannot even see (unknown id, or another firm's case).

Requires `notes:add_edit`.

delete.summary: Remove a note. Same author-or-admin rule as `putNote`; 204 with no body, and a second delete of the same id answers 404.

get.summary: Every assembled Chapter 7 packet of this case, newest first (issue #96).
get.description:
Packets are produced by the `packet_assembly` pipeline job: trigger one with `acceptCaseJob`, poll `getCaseJob` until it settles, and the succeeded job's `result` names the packet this listing also shows. Old packets stay listed — re-assembly creates rather than replaces.

Requires `cases:view_only`.

get.summary: A short-lived URL that serves one packet's bytes: the issue's "one download of the packet as filed-ready PDFs", a zip of the full form set plus the creditor matrix.
get.description:
The same ask-at-the-moment-of-use rule as `getDocumentUrl`: it expires in minutes and is a bearer capability, so never cache or log it.

Requires `cases:view_only`.

get.summary: The stored Chapter 13 plan's figures (issue 16.2 / #366): the waterfall by class and payee, feasibility, and the § 1325(a)(4) liquidation test, every figure naming the claim, plan field or rule it came from. The plan itself is the `plans` collection (`addCaseEntity` / `putCaseEntity`).
get.description:
Always resolves to 200 on a reachable case; read `PlanCalculation.problems` for what is still missing. A 404 means the case is unknown *or* not the caller's.

Requires `cases:view_only`.

post.summary: Unsaved alternatives, each calculated against the same case, in the order sent (at most five). Writes nothing: adopting one is an ordinary confirmed write of its body to `plans`. A malformed scenario is a 400 whose field paths read `scenarios[<n>].plan.<field>`.
post.description: Requires `cases:view_only`.

get.summary: Everyone ever invited to this case's client portal (ADR 0023), revoked included, oldest first.
get.description:
Needs `client_portal` at `view_only` — hidden by default for every role.

Requires `client_portal:view_only`.

delete.summary: Withdraw a client's access. Answers the binding, now `revoked`.

post.summary: Re-send an invitation that has not been used yet. A **409** means the client has already used the portal.
post.description: Requires `client_portal:add_edit`.

post.summary: Invite a debtor to this case's client portal. Cognito mails the temporary password; the API mails the context (which firm, where to sign in), and neither passes through here.
post.description:
Throws `ApiException` with status **409** when the roles are held by another client whose binding would be left with none, when the person already has live access to a case, or when the address has an Insolvia account that is not one of this firm's clients. Needs `client_portal` at `add_edit`.

Requires `client_portal:add_edit`.

get.summary: The published IRS National and Local Standards for the case's own jurisdiction and household (issue #348), for display beside Schedule J's health-care and transportation lines while a preparer types.
get.description:
Always resolves to 200; read `CaseStandards.problems` before rendering a `null` figure as zero — a case with no Debtor 1 or no county on file yet is simply too early for this lookup, not an error. Like `getCaseSummary`, a 404 means the case is unknown *or* not the caller's.

Requires `cases:view_only`.

get.summary: Every lifecycle move of the case, oldest first (issue #355). A 404 is `getCase`'s 404.
get.description: Requires `cases:view_only`.

get.summary: What this case is worth, what it owes, and whether it could be filed today.
get.description:
The case overview's one read. It is a separate endpoint rather than fields on `getCase` because it is expensive in a way the case record is not: every total is computed across the case's collections, so the server reads all of them. A caller who wants the chapter and district should call `getCase`.

`readyToFile` comes from the same gate `packet_assembly` runs, so it and the assembler cannot disagree. Like `getCase`, a 404 means the case is unknown *or* not the caller's.

Requires `cases:view_only`.

get.summary: Every task of one case, in the order they were added (a schedule's own order, not a worklist's — see `listMyTasks` for the one that sorts by due date).
get.description: Requires `tasks:view_only`.

post.summary: Add one task to a case (issue #356 / 14.4). Only `CreateTaskRequest.subject` is required.
post.description:
Throws `ApiValidationException` on a 400 — a missing `subject`, or an `assigneeSubject` naming somebody outside the caller's firm (checked against the same roster `listFirmUsers` reads). A plain `ApiException` (404) when the case is unknown or not the caller's.

Requires `tasks:add_edit`.

get.summary: One task. 404 if it, its case, or the case's firm is not the caller's.
get.description: Requires `tasks:view_only`.

patch.summary: Edit, reassign, complete or reopen a task; see `UpdateTaskRequest` for the three-state rule a `null` vs. an omitted key follows.
patch.description:
Throws `ApiValidationException` on a 400 — an empty request body, or `assigneeSubject` naming somebody outside the caller's firm.

Requires `tasks:add_edit`.

delete.summary: Remove a task. Answers 204 with no body.

get.summary: Every record of one collection in one case, in creation order (the order the rows were added, which holds still while someone works down the schedule).
get.description:
The wire body is `{"<collection>": [...]}`; this returns the array. No pagination — the answer is bounded by one case's schedule, and the server promises all of it.

Requires `intake:view_only`.

post.summary: Add one record to a generic case collection (issue #249): creditors, claims, assets, employments, income_summaries, households, expenses, dependents, codebtors, sofa_entries. The server mints the id and answers 201 with the stored record.
post.description:
The provenance rules are the debtor's, enforced identically: every populated field needs an entry (`staffTypedProvenance` builds the ordinary map), and machine-supplied values must be confirmed. Like `getCase`, a 404 means the case is unknown *or* not the caller's.

Requires `intake:add_edit`.

get.summary: One record. A 404 covers the unknown id, the foreign case, AND an id that belongs to a different collection of the same case — none are distinguishable, by the same anti-oracle rule `getCase` states.
get.description: Requires `intake:view_only`.

delete.summary: Remove one record. 204 with no body; a second delete of the same id answers 404.
delete.description:
References are not cascaded server-side: a claim naming a deleted creditor keeps its `creditor_id`, and the completeness gate (9.6) is where the dangling reference becomes an error.

Requires `intake:add_edit`.

get.summary: The court registry (issue #360): the districts and divisions a case may name, resolved as of today. Authenticated, every member of a firm, no feature gate; a caller in no firm is a 403 like everywhere else. Read-only — the registry is committed data the API ships (ADR 0014), and this is the list the create form's pickers read.
The firm's own record (issue #217).
get.description:
Administrators only (`firm_administration` at `view_only`). The name it returns is the same row `/v1/me` reads, so this is what every member's header already shows. See `Firm` for what the tenant shape deliberately does not carry.

Requires `firm_administration:view_only`.

patch.description:
`firm_administration` at `add_edit`. Name only — `UpdateFirmRequest` owns why `status` is absent and never joins. The new name reaches every member on their next `/v1/me`; nothing else needs invalidating. Throws `ApiValidationException` on a 400 with a per-field message.

Requires `firm_administration:add_edit`.

get.summary: The firm's whole client directory, archived clients included, ordered by surname then given name.
get.description:
Needs `clients` at `view_only`. Not access-logged (the list, like `GET /v1/cases`); every single-record call below is.

Requires `clients:view_only`.

post.summary: Add a person to the directory. The new client is `active`, and `created_by` is the caller.
post.description:
Needs `clients` at `add_edit`. Throws `ApiValidationException` on a 400 (per-field: `name`, `date_of_birth`, `residence_address.*`, `other_names_used[n].id`, …; `tax_id` if one was sent — it cannot be set here).

Requires `clients:add_edit`.

get.summary: One client. A 404 means the id is not in the caller's firm or does not exist — deliberately indistinguishable.
get.description: Requires `clients:view_only`.

put.summary: Replace a client's WHOLE editable record; see `FirmClientDraft`. The status, `created_by` and the tax ID are kept. Needs `clients` at `add_edit`.

get.summary: The client's cases THAT THE CALLER MAY SEE, newest first, each with the role the client holds (ADR 0022). A case the caller is not linked to is simply absent — the response never says how many were left out. A prospect's list is empty.
get.description:
Needs `clients` and `cases`, each at `view_only`. A 404 means the client is not in the caller's firm or does not exist.

Requires `clients:view_only` and `cases:view_only`.

post.summary: Fold `mergedId` INTO `survivorId` (ADR 0022). The survivor keeps its id; every case of the merged client — including ones the caller is not linked to — now names the survivor, the debtors' copied details unchanged; the merged client is archived with `merged_into`.
post.description:
Needs `clients` at `add_edit`. A 404 means the survivor is not in the caller's firm. Throws `ApiValidationException` on a 400 keyed `merged_client_id` (unknown client, or the same id twice), and a plain `ApiException` with `statusCode` **409** when either client is merged or archived, another merge involving either is in progress, or both are debtors on one case — its `message` says which. Nothing is written on any of these.

Requires `clients:add_edit`.

put.summary: Place a PROSPECT in the funnel, or take them out of it with `null` (issue #355). A 409 means the client has been retained (they have a case, or a retained date); a 404 that they are not in the caller's firm. Needs `clients: add_edit`.
Archive a client (`'archived'`) or bring one back (`'active'`). A status write, never a delete: there is no way to delete a client through this API (ADR 0022). Needs `clients` at `add_edit`.

get.summary: The firm's whole reusable creditor library (issue 13.9 / #350), for the case creditor form's picker and the `/firm/creditors` manager screen alike.
get.description:
Needs `creditor_library` at `view_only`.

Requires `creditor_library:view_only`.

post.summary: Add a creditor to the firm's library.
post.description:
Needs `creditor_library` at `add_edit`. Throws `ApiValidationException` on a 400 (per-field: `name`, `address.*`, `additional_notice_parties[n].*`).

Requires `creditor_library:add_edit`.

get.summary: One creditor in the firm's creditor library.
get.description: Requires `creditor_library:view_only`.

put.summary: Replace a library creditor's WHOLE record. See `LibraryCreditorDraft` for why this is PUT, not PATCH.
put.description:
A 404 means the id is not in the caller's firm's library or does not exist — deliberately indistinguishable, the same anti-oracle rule `updateFirmUser` follows.

Requires `creditor_library:add_edit`.

delete.summary: Remove a creditor from the library.
delete.description:
Removes the LIBRARY ROW ONLY. Every case creditor already copied from it keeps its own values — a library pick copies, it does not link (see `insolvia_core.library_creditors`) — so nothing already saved on a case changes.

Requires `creditor_library:add_edit`.

get.summary: Everyone in the caller's firm, as names.
get.description:
Available to anyone who can view cases, not only administrators, because this is what turns a subject into a person: `Case.createdBy` and every `CaseAssignee` are Cognito subjects, and without this the case list reads "opened by 00000000-0000-…".

Includes colleagues whose accounts are DISABLED. A case opened by somebody who has since left still names them, and dropping them here would turn that into an unresolvable id — this is for rendering history, not for populating a picker.

Throws `ApiException` (403) when the caller is in no firm, or their firm has not granted them `cases`.

Requires `cases:view_only`.

get.summary: The documents the firm asks every client for, and the shipped default beside them. `firm_administration` at `view_only`.
get.description: Requires `firm_administration:view_only`.

put.summary: Save the whole list. Throws `ApiValidationException` on a 400, keyed `items.<index>.<field>`. `firm_administration` at `add_edit`.

delete.summary: Back to the shipped default. Idempotent.

get.summary: The firm's own, case-less events (office events).
get.description: Requires `events:view_only`.

post.summary: `POST /v1/firm/events`
post.description: Requires `events:add_edit`.

get.summary: One event on the firm's calendar.
get.description: Requires `events:view_only`.

get.summary: Which questionnaire sections the firm's clients see, and the instructions they read (ADR 0023 PR 3). Every section, switched off or not: staff always see all of them.
get.description:
`firm_administration` at `view_only`, like `getFirm`.

Requires `firm_administration:view_only`.

put.summary: Save the whole config, every section once. Answers with what was stored, normalised (blank instructions read back as `null`). `firm_administration` at `add_edit`. Throws `ApiValidationException` on a 400, keyed `sections.<id>.<field>`.

delete.summary: Reset to the defaults: every section on, every instruction the catalogue's. Idempotent; answers with the default view. `firm_administration` at `add_edit`.

get.summary: The firm's whole staff list, with everything on it.
get.description:
Administrators only (`firm_administration`). For rendering a name, use `listFirmDirectory` instead: it needs no administrative permission and carries no email addresses.

Requires `firm_administration:view_only`.

post.summary: Add a colleague to the caller's firm.
post.description:
The server creates their Cognito account and emails them a temporary password; **nothing in this flow returns or reveals it**, here or on the server. There is no firm id in the request — the colleague joins the caller's own firm, which is not a value a client gets to choose.

Throws `ApiValidationException` on a 400 (per-field: `email`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `role`, `isAdmin`, `accessAllCases`, `permissions`), and a plain `ApiException` with status 409 when the address already has an Insolvia account.

Requires `firm_administration:add_edit`.

patch.description:
**`permissions` replaces the stored map** — see `UpdateFirmUserRequest`.

Throws `ApiException` with status **409** when the change would leave the firm with no active administrator. That is not a permission failure and should not be reported as one: self-signup is disabled, so such a firm could not appoint one back. Surface it as "appoint another administrator first".

A 404 means the subject is not in the caller's firm *or* does not exist — the two are deliberately indistinguishable.

Requires `firm_administration:add_edit`.

delete.summary: Remove a colleague from the firm.
delete.description:
**Removes the membership, not the person.** Their Cognito account survives, so what they get is a working sign-in and a 403 everywhere — the same state as somebody who has not been added yet. Disabling (`updateFirmUser(subject, { status: 'disabled' })`) is usually what a firm actually wants, because it keeps the record and the history.

409 when it would leave the firm with no active administrator; 404 when the subject is not in the caller's firm.

Requires `firm_administration:add_edit`.

get.summary: The signed-in caller's identity, and the app's "is my access token still good?" probe.
get.description:
Protected: sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from the configured `InsolviaApiClientOptions.accessToken` provider. Throws `ApiUnauthorizedException` when the API answers 401, and — without making a request at all — when there is no token to send.

Note the path is `/v1/me`, not `/me`: it is versioned like `/v1/waitlist`, and unlike the unversioned `/health`.

patch.description: Your name only; see `UpdateMeRequest` for why nothing else is self-service, and why either half alone is a legitimate body. Any ACTIVE firm member may call it — no permission level is required, which is the point of the endpoint. Answers with the same body as `me`, so the caller re-renders from the response instead of following up with a GET — which is also how a client holding a cached `/v1/me` refreshes it after a rename. Throws `ApiValidationException` on a 400 with a per-field message (`firstName` / `lastName`), and a plain `ApiException` with `statusCode` 403 for a caller in no firm — unlike the GET, which reports that state as an answer, there is no row to rename.

post.summary: Mint (or rotate) the caller's ICS feed token. The token is returned ONCE; `feedUrl` is the absolute address a calendar application subscribes to, and the only way to read it again is to mint a new one, which retires this one.
post.description: Requires `events:view_only`.

delete.summary: Revoke the feed; 404 when there is none.

get.summary: The caller's calendar as an iCalendar feed.
get.description: For calendar apps: authenticated by the `token` query parameter from `POST /v1/me/calendar-token`, or by a staff token when there is none. Covers a fixed window around today.

get.summary: The text to read (version, digest, body) and the caller's signature over it. Needs `electronic_filing` at `view_only`.
get.description: Requires `electronic_filing:view_only`.

post.summary: Sign the text the caller was shown, named by the `version` and `digest` it came with. Throws `ApiReauthenticationRequiredException` when the caller's sign-in is not recent (minutes, not the session's age): sign in again with a forced prompt, then retry. A 409 means the text changed, or it is already signed. Needs `electronic_filing` at `add_edit`.
post.description: Requires `electronic_filing:add_edit`.

delete.summary: Withdraw the signature, which DESTROYS every filing credential the caller holds. Resolves to how many were destroyed. A 404 means nothing was signed.

get.summary: The caller's OWN credentials in the vault, as status views: never a password, never a seed. Needs `electronic_filing` at `view_only` (hidden for every role by default).
get.description: Requires `electronic_filing:view_only`.

post.summary: Seal and store one credential for the caller. The server answers the status view; nothing sent is echoed. Throws `ApiValidationException` on a 400 (per field: `login`, `password`, `totp_seed`, `courts`) and a 409 when that login is already enrolled. Needs `electronic_filing` at `add_edit`.
post.description: Requires `electronic_filing:add_edit`.

delete.summary: Revoke: the server DESTROYS the sealed credential, and the filing worker can no longer open it. A 404 means the caller has no such credential.

get.summary: Every task across every case in the caller's firm they can reach, sorted soonest-due-first (undated tasks last).
get.description:
`options.scope` (default `'mine'`) narrows to tasks assigned to the caller; `'firm'` is the dashboard's firm-wide toggle — see `ListMyTasksOptions`.

**Never leaks a task from a case outside the caller's reach, in either scope** — the server walks the same reachable-case listing `listCases` uses (`api/routes/tasks.py`'s module docstring owns the argument), so this is safe to call before the caller has opened any particular case.

Requires `tasks:view_only`.

get.summary: The CLIENT's own answers, every status: the questionnaire's resume state (ADR 0023 PR 4). Only this client's, and only in sections the firm still shows. Portal token, like `getPortalMe`.

post.summary: Answer one question. The answer is a candidate in the firm's review queue, never case data. Throws `ApiValidationException` on a 400, keyed `value.<input key>`, `questionId` (not in this client's questionnaire — including a section the firm switched off) or `filingRole`; a plain `ApiException` with 409 when a one-answer question already has a pending answer (change that one with `updatePortalAnswer`).

put.summary: Change a PENDING answer's value. 409 once the firm has reviewed it (a change is then a new answer); 404 for anything that is not this client's own.

delete.summary: Withdraw a PENDING answer. The row is kept, `withdrawn`; 409 once reviewed, 404 if not this client's.

get.summary: The CLIENT side: what the firm asked this client for, each with their own uploads against it, and the progress. Called with a portal session's token.

post.summary: Step one of a client's upload, against one request. Prefer `uploadPortalDocument`, which runs all three steps for the reason `uploadDocument` gives.
Confirm the PUT; this is what marks the request received. 409 when the bytes never arrived (`isUploadIncomplete`).

get.summary: The CLIENT side (ADR 0023). Construct the client with the PORTAL session's token for this one: a staff token answers **401** here, and a portal token answers 401 on every staff method. A **403** means the signed-in person has no live access to a case.

The CLIENT side (ADR 0023 PR 3): the sections this client's firm shows them, in order, each with the instructions in force. A section the firm switched off is absent. Called with a portal session's token, like `getPortalMe`.

post.summary: Stop marketing email to the address a signed unsubscribe token names.
post.description: The token comes from the link in an email; the address itself is never sent. Answers 202 once the address is suppressed.

post.summary: Submit a waitlist entry.
post.description: Returns the server's confirmation on 201. Throws `ApiValidationException` on a 400 with per-field messages.
