counterparty_name.description: One free-text line — counterparties are predominantly entities.

description.description: What the contract or lease is for, term remaining, contract number.

intention.description: Form 108's own column, NOT printed on 106G itself — stored here so the B108 projection (13.10) reads it rather than asking again.

list_on_statement_of_intention.description: Whether this row belongs on the Statement of Intention at all.

community_state.description: The community property state lived in — a two-letter code.

ApplyChecklistResult.description: `POST .../document-requests/from-checklist` — the list after, and how many it added.

AssetExemptionClaim.description: One exemption record on an asset, and what the server counts it as.

knownStatute.description: False when the citation is not in the effective scheme's table.

AssetExemptionFigures.description: One asset's equity and what the claims on it cover. `currentValue`, `netEquity` and `unexempt` are `null` while the asset has no value typed; `homesteadCap` is the § 522(p) cap where it binds this asset and `capApplied` says the claims exceeded it. `suggestions` is the default amount for a NEW claim under each entry id — the lesser of the unexempt equity and the statute's remaining room — so the screen never subtracts.

AssetLiens.description: What one asset carries: its secured claims, and the sum of their amounts.

securedTotal.description: Column A's amounts summed — what is owed against the property.

CalendarEvent.description:
One calendar event — a case's (`case_id` present) or the firm's own.

`all_day` decides how `start`/`end` read: form dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`, `end` INCLUSIVE) when true, RFC 3339 UTC instants (`...Z`) when false.

`generated` events were written by the deadline engine from the case's filed and § 341 dates and name their rule (`rule_id`, `rule_citation`). They cannot be edited or deleted — only DISMISSED, which is what `InsolviaApiClient.dismissCaseEvent` does — and a dismissal survives regeneration.

attendees.description: Firm-user subjects — resolve them through the directory.

CalendarEventDraft.description:
The `POST`/`PUT` body for a hand-made event — a WHOLE record, never a partial PATCH, for the same reason `LibraryCreditorDraft` is one.

`start` alone is enough: a bare date makes an all-day event ending the same day; an instant makes a timed one ending an hour later. `all_day` only needs stating when `start`'s shape would guess wrong.

CalendarTokenMinted.description: `POST /v1/me/calendar-token` — the new feed token and the path that carries it.

feedPath.description: `/v1/me/calendar.ics?token=…`, relative to the API's base URL.

CandidateOrigin.description: Which surface wrote a candidate, and as whom — never client-claimed.

channel.description: `client` is a debtor answering through the client portal (ADR 0023).

clientId.description: The model that extracted it, or the harness's OAuth client id.

subject.description: The subject it is attributed to — resolve through the firm directory.

CandidateQuestion.description: The question a client-answered candidate answers.

CandidateStatus.description: Where a candidate sits. `pending` awaits a human; `accepted`, `corrected` and `rejected` are review outcomes (retained — they are the extraction quality feedback loop); `withdrawn` is the proposer's own retraction, an MCP-surface act.

Case.description:
A case, as returned by every `/v1/cases` endpoint: `{"id", "createdBy", "chapter", "district", "status", "createdAt", "updatedAt"}`.

**There is no `firmId`.** Every caller who can see a case is in its firm by construction, so the id would echo the reader's own tenant back at them.

id.description: The server-generated case id.

createdBy.description:
The subject of the firm user who OPENED the matter — an audit fact, not a permission. It grants nothing: reaching a case means being in its firm and either an admin, or carrying `FirmMembership.accessAllCases`, or being linked to it.

Keyed the same way `FirmColleague.subject` is, so `listFirmDirectory` turns it into a name. Rendering it raw is a bug — it is a UUID.

district.description: The filing district's printed name (`"Middle District of Florida"`) — DERIVED by the server from `court` (issue #360), never sent. On a case written before the court registry existed it is whatever free text was typed, and `court` is absent: that is how a client learns the case still needs a court chosen.

court.description: The court's CM/ECF code (`"flmb"`) — a reference into `CourtRegistry`. Absent on a pre-registry case.

division.description: The division's code within the court (`"tampa"`). Absent with `court`.

status.description: Where the case sits in the filing workflow.

createdAt.description: The server's UTC creation timestamp, kept verbatim as the wire string.

updatedAt.description: The server's UTC last-update timestamp, kept verbatim as the wire string.

formRevisions.description: The effective-dating pins packet assembly wrote (issue #96): form series id -> the pinned revision (`effective_date[+sequence]`). **Absent until the first packet assembles** — a floating case records nothing — and replaced whole on re-assembly. Read-only: no request ever sends it.

constantsSetId.description: The pinned `code/dollar-amounts` release id. Reserved — the series has no registry yet (it lands with the means-test milestone), so today this is always absent.

exemptionSet.description: 106C line 1's election (issue #346). **Absent until chosen** through `UpdateCaseChanges.exemptionSet`; in an opt-out state the law forces the answer whether or not one is stored, and `ExemptionAnalysis.election.effective` is what was actually used.

filedAt.description: The petition date — the order for relief in a voluntary case — as a form date, `YYYY-MM-DD` (issue 14.6 / #358). **Absent until recorded** through `UpdateCaseChanges.filedAt`; setting it is what populates the case's generated deadlines.

meeting341At.description: The FIRST date the court set for the § 341(a) meeting of creditors, as a form date. Absent until recorded; the 60-day objection windows and the rest of the meeting-anchored deadlines count from it.

caseNumber.description: The court's case number, as the notice of filing prints it (`8:26-bk-01234`). Absent until recorded; a case cannot reach `filed` without it.

judge.description: The assigned judge's name. Absent until recorded.

trustee.description: The case trustee's name. Absent until recorded.

officeFileNumber.description: The firm's own file number for the matter. Absent until recorded.

archivedAt.description: When the case was archived — out of the working list (`listCases()`), into the archive (`listCases({ archived: true })`). Absent on a case in the working list.

archivedBy.description: The firm user's subject who archived it; present with `archivedAt`.

CaseAssignee.description: One person linked to a case, as `GET /v1/cases/{id}/assignees` returns them.

subject.description: The colleague's Cognito subject — resolve it through the directory.

assignedAt.description: When the link was made, verbatim.

assignedBy.description: The subject of whoever made it.

CaseChapter.description: The bankruptcy chapter a case is filed under. A union of numeric literals rather than `number`, so an invalid chapter is a compile error at the call site, not just a server-side rejection.

CaseEntityList.description: One collection's records, under the collection's own name: `GET /v1/cases/{caseId}/creditors` answers `{"creditors": [...]}`.

CaseForm.description:
One row of `GET /v1/cases/{caseId}/forms` — a form this case's chapter and pin require (the server's `packet_form_series`, never re-derived here), what it is called, its one metric where the hub defines one for it (Schedules A/B-H count the entities they print; I and J total a dollar figure; every other form carries none), and the slice of the completeness gate's problem list that belongs to it.

`series` is the `form/<x>` id packet assembly also uses (`Packet.formRevisions`'s keys); `form` is the short key this same row's preview URL takes (`InsolviaApiClient.getCaseFormPreview`).

metric.description: Absent, never null, for a form the hub defines no metric for.

problems.description: Empty when this form has nothing blocking it.

openTaskCount.description: Not-done tasks (issue #356 / 14.4) anchored to this form via `Task.formSeries` — always present, `0` included, unlike `metric` which some forms genuinely have none of.

CaseLiens.description: `GET /v1/cases/{caseId}/liens`, and the `liens` member of the summary — every secured claim's figures, and every asset that carries a lien. An asset with no linked claim is absent rather than listed at zero.

CaseMeansTest.description:
`GET /v1/cases/{caseId}/means-test` — the § 707(b) trace for one case as of its expected filing date (issue #349), run by the SAME code path the packet's B122A-1 and B122A-2 use. Nothing here is for the client to add up: every figure names the rule, input or dataset release it came from.

Always 200. `outcome` is `undetermined` with the reasons in `problems` while the case is too early to answer (no household entered yet, a planned filing date the datasets do not cover); `comparison` is `null` then, and for an exempt debtor whose household is not entered. `lines` is empty below the median and for an exempt debtor on Chapter 7 — Form 122A-2 is not filed in either case. On a Chapter 13 case (issue #365) the same endpoint runs § 1325(b): `chapter13` carries the verdict, and `lines` holds B122C-1's Part 2-3 lines always, plus B122C-2's above the median.

chapter.description: The case's chapter — which calculation ran.

releaseIds.description: Series id → release id, for every dataset the run read.

CaseProblem.description:
One reason a case cannot assemble its filing packet as it stands.

`source` says where the fix belongs: a collection name (`"claims"`, `"households"`), `"case"` or `"debtors"` for the two non-generic records, or a form series id (`"form/b101"`) when a projection is what refuses. `itemId` names the record when one record owns the fix, and `field` is the body path the entity endpoints validate — so a screen can send someone to the exact input rather than to "the case is incomplete". Both are absent, never null, where the problem belongs to a whole collection.

The same shape the `packet_assembly` job reports when it refuses, because it is the same gate: see `CaseSummary.readyToFile`.

CaseStandards.description:
`GET /v1/cases/{caseId}/standards` — the published IRS allowances beside Schedule J's health-care and transportation lines, for the case's own jurisdiction and household (issue #348).

NOT the means test: `state`/`county`/`householdSize` here come from Debtor 1's residence address and the dependents recorded as living with the debtor — the best facts on file while the workbench is being typed — not the confirmed household composition the means test itself asks for. The two are allowed to disagree.

Always 200 with whichever figures resolved. `problems` explains any that did not (no Debtor 1 yet, no county on file, a state the Local Standards launch set does not cover) — read it before rendering a `null` figure as zero.

CaseStatusChange.description: One move in a case's lifecycle, from `GET /v1/cases/{caseId}/status-history` (issue #355): who moved it, when, from what to what.

changedBy.description: A firm user's subject — resolve it with `listFirmDirectory` — or `FILING_WORKER_ACTOR` when the filing worker filed the case (ADR 0024 PR 8).

filingId.description: The electronic filing that made this move; absent on a person's edit.

CaseSummary.description:
`GET /v1/cases/{caseId}/summary` — one case from above.

`readyToFile` is the SAME completeness gate packet assembly runs, not a cheaper approximation of it, so a screen showing "ready" can never be contradicted by the assembler a click later. When it is `false`, `problems` is why and is never empty.

Expensive relative to `Case`: the totals are computed from the case's collections, so this reads all of them. Fetch it for a case overview, not to learn a chapter.

liens.description: The same block `getCaseLiens` returns, for the overview.

CaseTotals.description:
What a case is worth and what it owes — **every figure a decimal STRING**.

Strings and not numbers, all the way from the server: these are amounts on a bankruptcy filing, and JSON numbers arrive as IEEE doubles where `1234.05` does not survive the trip. The same reason the domain stores a claim's `amount` as a string.

**Do not add these up in a client.** They are already the totals, computed from the same functions the official forms print from — `secured` is what B106D's Column A totals, the unsecured pair is B106E/F lines 6e and 6j, and the asset pair is B106A/B lines 55 and 62. A second sum computed in a screen is a second answer to "what does this debtor owe", and the two agree only until somebody edits one.

totalExempt.description: The plain sum of the case's exemption claim amounts — NOT the exemption law's arithmetic (the homestead cap, a "100% of fair market value" election). Issue #346 owns that; this is deliberately just a sum.

totalNonExempt.description: `assets` minus `totalExempt`, not floored at zero — an exemption claimed larger than the property is a fact worth a negative figure showing, not hiding.

monthlyIncome.description: 106I line 12 — the same figure that form prints.

monthlyExpenses.description: 106J line 22c — likewise the schedule's own figure.

monthlyExcess.description: `monthlyIncome` minus `monthlyExpenses` — the Chapter 13 plan's starting number, shown on both the income and expenses screens (issue #348). Can be negative; a decimal STRING like every other figure here, so render it as given rather than parsing and re-formatting it.

ChecklistItem.description: One document a firm asks for — a checklist entry.

kind.description: The kind an upload against it is filed under.

ChecklistItemStatus.description: A checklist line's state. `action` is a step the attorney takes outside Insolvia; `confirm` is a court fact the registry has not verified.

ClaimLien.description:
One secured claim's collateral, resolved, and its two portions — the server's `core/liens.py` figures (issue #345), the same ones B106D's Column B prints from. **Every money member is a decimal STRING** and is already the answer: a screen shows these, never recomputes them.

`collateralDescription` and `collateralValue` are the RESOLVED values (the claim's typed override where there is one, the linked asset's otherwise). A portion is absent, never null, while it cannot be derived yet — no amount, or no collateral value from either source — so `=== undefined` is the whole "not known yet" check.

seniorLiens.description: The amounts of the liens senior to this one on the same asset.

ClientRole.description: Which debtor a portal client answers for. Never `non_filing_spouse` — who has no login in v1.

CmiColumn.description: One B122A-1 column: A is Debtor 1, B is Debtor 2 or the spouse.

excluded.description: The § 101(10A)(B)(ii) receipts — recorded, shown, never counted.

CmiEntry.description: One dated receipt behind a CMI line — the derivation's atoms.

CmiGap.description: A window month with no paycheck from an employment that should have one.

CmiLine.description: One B122A-1 income line of one column, as `core/cmi.py` derived it: the six-month total, the monthly average the form prints, and every entry behind them. `note` explains line-level arithmetic (the business/rental expense subtraction, an entered override); `citation` is set on an excluded line. The two extra averages appear only on business and rental lines.

CmiTrace.description: The § 101(10A) derivation, line by line — `core/cmi.py`'s result.

CmiWindow.description: The six-month lookback the derivation read the records over.

courtId.description: The PACER court id (`FLMBK`), or `null` where the lookup did not carry one.

name.description: The printed name — what `Case.district` is derived as.

caseUpload.description: Whether the court's Case Upload facility has been proven for our packages.

officeCode.description: The digit before the colon in the case number, or `null` where unverified.

counties.description: The counties whose debtors file here, by FIPS-5 code.

CourtRegistry.description: The court registry — `GET /v1/courts` (issue #360): the districts and divisions a case may name, from the `courts/us-bankruptcy` series the API ships (ADR 0014, ADR 0024). Read-only; every member of a firm may read it.

CreateCaseBody.description: `POST /v1/cases` as sent. The client's `CreateCaseRequest` says `clientIds`; the wire says `client_ids`.

client_ids.description: The firm clients the case is for: Debtor 1, then Debtor 2 on a joint case.

CreateDocumentRequest.description:
The `POST /v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` request body: `{"kind", "fileName", "contentType", "byteSize"}`, all four required, and `requestId` when the upload answers one of the case's document requests.

`contentType` and `byteSize` are validated here and then **bound into the presigned signature**, so they are not merely declarations: an upload whose body is a different length, or whose `Content-Type` header differs, is refused by S3 with a signature error the client cannot interpret. Send the real values.

There is no `provenance` field and the API refuses one: provenance describes values extracted *from* a document, not the document itself.

kind.description: What the uploader says this is.

fileName.description: The file name, 1-255 characters, no path separators or invisible characters.

contentType.description: The media type, lowercase, from the allowlist.

byteSize.description: The exact size of the bytes to be uploaded, 1..`MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTE_SIZE`.

requestId.description: The case's document request this upload answers. Completing the upload marks it received. A waived request is refused (400 on `requestId`).

CreateTaskRequest.description: The `POST /v1/cases/{caseId}/tasks` request body. Only `subject` is required — everything else is filled in later with `InsolviaApiClient.updateTask`. `done` is never accepted here: every task starts not-done.

CreditorMatrix.description: `GET /v1/cases/{caseId}/creditor-matrix` — the court's mailing list, or every reason there isn't one yet. `content` is the exact text of the .txt file (CRLF line endings, plain ASCII) and is present only when `problems` is empty: the server refuses to produce a partial matrix, because a missing entry is a bankruptcy notice that never arrives. The court-format rules the server enforces are cited in `services/api/src/insolvia_api/core/creditor_matrix.py`.

fileName.description: The suggested file name for the download, `creditor-matrix.txt`.

creditorCount.description: Entries printed — after identical blocks are deduplicated.

duplicatesOmitted.description: Blocks dropped because they would print identically to another.

content.description: The file text. Absent, never null, while `problems` is non-empty.

CreditorMatrixProblem.description:
One reason one creditor cannot go on the matrix as recorded — issue #94.

`creditorId` is absent on the single case-level problem (a case with no creditors at all); `field` is the creditor body path the fix belongs to (`name`, `address.state`, ...), so a screen can put the message next to the input that needs the edit.

Debtor.description:
A debtor as both endpoints return it: identity, `provenance`, and whatever of `DebtorBody` is populated.

**Absent members are absent, not null.** On a progressive intake most of the record is empty most of the time, and the API omits empty values — and empty sub-objects and empty lists — entirely rather than sending a body of nulls. This model mirrors that: a missing `name` means nothing in the name has been filled in yet, and the key is genuinely not there.

id.description: The server-generated debtor id, stable across saves.

tax_id.description: The last-four view — never the number. See `TaxIdView`.

case_id.description: The case this debtor belongs to.

filing_role.description: Which debtor of the case this is.

created_at.description: The server's UTC creation timestamp, kept verbatim as the wire string.

updated_at.description: The server's UTC last-update timestamp, kept verbatim as the wire string.

client_id.description: The `FirmClient` this debtor is (ADR 0022) — present on every Debtor 1 and Debtor 2 opened since cases are opened for clients, and on a non-filing spouse who is a client. **Server-owned**: `putDebtor` never sends it and the server keeps it; re-linking is `linkDebtorClient`.

differs_from_client.description: The copied field paths where this case's debtor and the linked client record now disagree (`name.given`, `residence_address.county`, …) — computed on read, never stored. `[]` means identical. Absent when the debtor names no client, or when the caller cannot see the firm's client directory.

provenance.description: Where each populated field came from. **Always present**, unlike every other optional member here — the API emits it unconditionally, as `{}` on a record with nothing in it.

other_names_used.description: Aliases used in the last 8 years. Each row needs a client-chosen `OtherName.id`.

employer_ids.description: Employer identification numbers. Each max 20 characters.

signed_at.description: The signature date, `YYYY-MM-DD` — a calendar fact, not an instant, so no time and no zone (see docs/reference/case-data-model.md). The API parses it as a real date and rejects anything else, including a timestamp and the compact `20260805` form. `DateInput` in `@insolvia-ai/design-system` emits exactly this.

Document.description:
A document of a case, as `document_json` renders it: `{"id", "caseId", "kind", "fileName", "contentType", "byteSize", "uploadedAt", "status"}`.

`uploadedBy`, `storageRef` and `etag` are stored server-side and deliberately not in the body — the object key and its etag are the API's business, and a client that knew the layout could come to depend on it.

`kind` and `contentType` are plain strings here while the
*request* models use the unions above, and the asymmetry is deliberate: a value the caller is about to send should be a compile error when it is not one the API accepts, but a value the API sends back must not be able to break decoding of a whole page of documents if the server's allowlist ever grows. `status` is the exception — a closed two-value set the UI branches on, where an unrecognised value means the client cannot tell "you can open this" from "this never uploaded", and failing loudly beats guessing.

id.description: The server-generated document id.

caseId.description: The case this document belongs to.

kind.description: The uploader's claim about what this is — see `DOCUMENT_KINDS`.

fileName.description: The uploader's file name, for display and as a download name.

contentType.description: The validated, lowercased media type — see `DOCUMENT_CONTENT_TYPES`.

byteSize.description: The size in bytes. **Its meaning changes with `status`**: on a `'pending'` record it is what the client said it would send, on a `'stored'` one it is what S3 counted.

uploadedAt.description: When the upload was **authorised** — not when the bytes landed. The server's UTC millisecond-precision ISO-8601 `Z` string, kept verbatim.

status.description: Whether the bytes are known to be in the bucket.

channel.description: Who uploaded it, as a class: a firm user, or the client through the portal (ADR 0023). A client's upload is never auto-extracted.

requestId.description: The case's `DocumentRequest` this upload answers, or `null`.

DocumentDownload.description:
The `GET /v1/cases/{caseId}/documents/{documentId}/url` 200 response: `{"url", "method", "expiresAt"}` — a short-lived capability to read one document's bytes.

Minted on request rather than attached to every listed document, so one of these means one document was actually fetched. It expires in minutes; ask again rather than caching it.

url.description: The presigned URL. A bearer capability — do not log it.

method.description: The one verb the signature permits — `GET`.

expiresAt.description: When the URL stops working, as a UTC ISO-8601 `Z` string.

DocumentRequest.description: One document asked of a case's client — the staff view.

documentIds.description: The completed uploads against it, in the order they completed.

receivedAt.description: When the first upload against it completed; kept if it is reopened.

DocumentRequestProgress.description: Arrived against outstanding. `total` excludes waived requests.

DocumentUpload.description:
The capability minted alongside a new document record: one HTTP request, to one object, for a few minutes.

**`headers` is passed through untouched and is not a fixed shape.** The server chooses which headers it signs (today: `Content-Type` and the tag that makes an unconfirmed upload reapable — deliberately no encryption header, the bucket's default supplies that), and S3 checks every one. Modelling it as an interface with named keys would mean a header added server-side was silently dropped by every deployed client, turning every upload into a 403 that looks like a bug here. Send this map verbatim, add nothing, and in particular never add an `Authorization` header — the URL is already the credential, and one more would invalidate it.

`Content-Length` is signed too and is deliberately *not* in this map: every HTTP client sets it from the body, and browsers forbid JavaScript from setting it at all.

url.description: The presigned URL. Treat it as a secret: it is a bearer capability.

method.description: The one verb the signature permits — `PUT`.

headers.description: The exact headers the signature demands. Send all of them, change none.

expiresAt.description: When the URL stops working, as a UTC ISO-8601 `Z` string.

ExemptionAnalysis.description:
`GET /v1/cases/{caseId}/exemption-analysis` — the Schedule C workbench's read (issue #346): the registry table this case may claim under, drawn down by its own claims, and every asset's value − liens − claimed.

Always 200. `problems` lists what stopped a figure resolving (no debtor state, an unsupported state, no election yet); `warnings` what to check before claiming (the § 522(b)(3)(A) domicile rule, a claim citing a statute outside the scheme). Nothing here is recomputed in a screen.

ExemptionElection.description: 106C line 1 as the server resolved it. `stored` is the case record's answer; `effective` is what the analysis used — the same where the law allows it, the state scheme where the state has opted out, and `null` where a choice is still owed (then `entries` is empty and `problems` says so). `optedOut` is `null` when the state is unknown or unsupported.

ExemptionElectionOption.description: One answer the case may store for 106C line 1, and the scheme it means.

ExemptionEntryAvailability.description: One claimable statute under the effective scheme, and what this case has left under it. **Every money member is a decimal STRING.** `limit` and `available` are `null` where the registry states no flat cap (an unlimited homestead, a "reasonably necessary for support" entry). `carryover` is the part of a wildcard's limit that is unused homestead carried over. Over-claiming shows as `available: "0.00"`, never an error.

citation.description: The registry's citation — what a claim's `statute_citation` should carry.

ExemptionLookbacks.description: The § 522 lookback windows as calendar dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`), computed from the resolution date: (o) ten years, (p) 1,215 days, (q) five years, and the § 522(b)(3)(A) 730-day domicile period.

ExtractionCandidate.description: One row of a case's review queue: a machine-proposed record awaiting (or past) human confirmation. `payload` is the proposed record in the target collection's own body shape; the server re-validates whatever comes back, so the loose typing here never becomes a write.

documentId.description: The source document, when the extraction stream wrote this row.

confidence.description: The model's certainty, 0-1, extraction rows only.

locatorPage.description: 1-based page of the source document the record was read from.

question.description: For a client's portal answer (origin channel `client`): the question it answers, in the words the client read, and the debtor it is for.

client.description: For a client's portal answer: who the FIRM says gave it — the name on the invitation, never anything the client's token says.

approvedBy.description: The approving attorney's subject — always the login's owner.

FilingApprovalBasis.description: WHAT THE ATTORNEY IS SHOWN, and approves: the court, the documents in docket order with their sizes and digests, the checklist, the fee handling, and `digest` over all of it plus the case record behind it (`services/api core/filing_approval.py` defines it). Approve by posting back exactly this `digest` — the server refuses any other.

scheme.description: `insolvia-filing-approval/1` — what the digest covers, by name.

fee.description: Today always the hand-back: Insolvia enters no card details.

signInMaxAgeSeconds.description: How recent the sign-in must be to approve (seconds).

approvalTtlSeconds.description: How long an approval waits for the filing worker before expiring (seconds).

FilingApprovalDocument.description: One document of what an approval would cover, in docket order.

file.description: Absent for a document prepared outside Insolvia.

FilingApprovalFile.description: One packet file as the assembly worker measured it — what an approval binds each document to (ADR 0024 build PR 6).

pageCount.description: Absent for the creditor matrix (a text file).

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file's bytes, lower-case hex; absent on a packet assembled before PR 6.

FilingApprovalStatus.description: `pending` until the filing worker uses it (`consumed`, once), or it is `voided`, or it lapses (`expired`).

FilingApprovalView.description: `GET`/`POST`/`DELETE /v1/cases/{caseId}/filing-approval` (ADR 0024, guardrail 1): what would be approved, and the case's current approval (absent when there has never been one).

filing.description: The approval's filing, once the filing worker has claimed it (ADR 0024 PR 8).

FilingApprovalVoidReason.description: Why an approval was voided. `changed`: the filing set is not what was approved.

FilingAuthorizationSignature.description: The caller's signature, as `GET /v1/me/filing-authorization` shows it.

FilingAuthorizationStatus.description: `GET`/`POST /v1/me/filing-authorization` — the text, and the caller's signature over it. `current` is false with no signature, and false with a signature over an OLDER text version (`signature.text_version !== current_version`): a new version invalidates older signatures, and nothing can be enrolled or filed until it is signed. Snake_case, as `insolvia_core.filing_authorization.authorization_json` writes it.

FilingAuthorizationText.description: The filing authorization's text as it ships (ADR 0024, guardrail 2): render `text` exactly, and sign by posting back `version` and `digest` — the server refuses any other pair, so a stale screen cannot sign a text the attorney never saw.

digest.description: SHA-256 of `text`'s UTF-8 bytes, lower-case hex.

link.description: An app segment under `/cases/{caseId}/` (`''` is the case overview) — absent when the step happens outside Insolvia.

FilingConfirmation.description: What the court's confirmation screen said.

filedAt.description: The court's own timestamp, as printed.

FilingCredential.description: One of the caller's own CM/ECF credentials in the vault (ADR 0024, guardrail 3) — `GET /v1/me/filing-credentials`, gated by `electronic_filing`. THE STATUS VIEW, and all a client ever receives: no password, no TOTP seed, nothing sealed. Snake_case, as `insolvia_core.filing_credentials.credential_json` writes it.

courts.description: Court codes (`txsb`, …) the attorney says they e-file in.

status.description: `active` is the only stored status: revoking DELETES the credential.

FilingDocument.description: One document of the filing set, in the court's docket order.

fileName.description: The name to upload it under — the packet zip's own unless the court prescribes one.

source.description: `packet`: in Insolvia's packet zip. `outside`: prepared outside Insolvia.

note.description: Absent when there is nothing to add.

FilingDocumentHandling.description: How a document reaches the docket: uploaded as listed (`file`), as an event of its own, under the court's restricted SSN-statement event (B121), or not at all (B121 in a court that takes the number on its opening screen instead).

FilingHandBack.description: Why the worker stopped and what the attorney does next, in words.

courtSaid.description: The court's own message, when there was one.

FilingRecord.description: One filing record, as `GET .../filing-approval` serves it.

attorneyId.description: The attorney whose login it used — the only one who may resolve it.

resolvable.description: Whether the attorney may still resolve it.

receiptDocumentId.description: The stored court-filing receipt, a case document.

FilingResolution.description: The attorney's recorded answer to a hand-back.

docketCheckedAt.description: When they confirmed they checked the court's docket.

FilingResolutionOutcome.description: `filed`: the court has it. `not_filed`: it does not — the case is free to approve again.

FilingSet.description: `GET /v1/cases/{caseId}/filing-set` (ADR 0024 build PR 3) — the documents the attorney files, in the court's docket order and names, each checked against the court's file rules, and the hand-off checklist built from the case record. Files nothing; carries no tax identifier.

court.description: Absent when the case names no court from the registry.

filingMethod.description: Always `hand_off` until a court's filing driver is verified.

packet.description: The filing-set packet the checks judged; absent when none is assembled.

FilingSetBasis.description: Where a per-court figure came from: the court (verified or not), or the common default.

FilingSetCheckName.description: Which of the three file checks a `FilingSetCheck` is.

FilingSetCheckOutcome.description: A check's result. `unmeasured` means nobody has measured the file — no filing-set packet yet, a packet from before measurement, or a document prepared outside Insolvia — never "it passed".

FilingState.description: The filing worker's states (`insolvia_core.filings`). `handed_back`, `outcome_unknown` and `filed` are terminal; the first two are what the attorney resolves.

Firm.description:
The firm's own record — `GET /v1/firm` and `PATCH /v1/firm`, for the firm's administrators.

Thinner than what the ADMIN portal sees, deliberately: the provenance fields (`createdBy`, `createdByEmail`) name the Insolvia staff member who provisioned the firm, and a staff identity is not something a tenant response carries.

createdAt.description: When the firm was provisioned, verbatim.

updatedAt.description: Last write to the record, verbatim.

defaultCourt.description: The firm's defaults for a new case (issue #360): explicit `null` until set.

letterhead.description: The firm's letterhead, or `null` until set.

FirmClient.description:
A person in the firm's client directory — `/v1/firm/clients`, gated by the `clients` feature. One client has many cases over time; a prospect is a client with no case yet.

**Snake_case**, for `LibraryCreditor`'s reason: the identity fields are the case domain's own shapes (`PersonName`, `Address`, `OtherName`), reused verbatim so a client copied onto a debtor needs no mapping. Absent optional fields are omitted by the server, never `null`.

name.description: Always present; at least one of `surname` / `given` is set.

lead_source.description: Free text in v1; a firm pick-list is a later issue.

tax_id_last_four.description: The last four digits of the client's tax ID — the only tax-ID fact any response carries. It cannot be set through this API: the full value is sealed once and entered on a case.

merged_into.description: Present only on a client that was MERGED into another (ADR 0022): the surviving client's id. Such a client is `archived` for good — it cannot be edited, restored, merged again or opened for a case; its cases now belong to the survivor.

prospect_stage.description: Where a PROSPECT sits in the funnel (issue #355) — present only while `first_retained_at` is absent and a stage has been set through `setFirmClientProspectStage`. Server-owned: the whole-record PUT never sends it.

created_by.description: The subject of the firm user who created the record.

FirmClientCase.description: One entry of `GET /v1/firm/clients/{id}/cases` (ADR 0022): a case the caller may see, and which debtor of it the client is.

FirmClientDraft.description: The `POST` / `PUT /v1/firm/clients/{id}` body — a WHOLE record, never a partial PATCH (`LibraryCreditorDraft`'s reason): a field omitted from a PUT is cleared. `status`, `created_by` and the tax ID are the server's and are not part of the draft; archive with `setFirmClientStatus`.

other_names_used.description: Each row needs its own client-chosen `id`, as a debtor's does.

FirmClientStatus.description: `archived` leaves the person in the directory — archiving is a status write, never a delete (ADR 0022).

FirmColleague.description:
A colleague as `GET /v1/firm/directory` returns them — three fields, for every member of the firm.

Deliberately thinner than `FirmUser`. It exists so a subject (`Case.createdBy`, an assignee) can be rendered as a name, and that need does not extend to a colleague's email address or permission map.

subject.description: The Cognito subject other endpoints address them by.

firstName.description: The two halves of their name. Either may be `''` — see `FirmMembership`.

displayName.description: Their composed name, for display. Server-derived.

signatureBlock.description: Their standing signature block, or `null` (issue #360) — the one field beyond identity every colleague may see, because the petition screen's "use firm default" is case work and a bar number is on every filing.

FirmDocumentChecklist.description: `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /v1/firm/document-checklist`. `isDefault` means the firm has stored nothing and the shipped default is in force; `defaultItems` is that default, always present, so a screen can offer it.

FirmMembership.description:
The caller's own firm and standing in it — the `firm` block of `GET /v1/me`.

**Absent, not null, when the caller is in no firm.** A person can sign in before anyone adds them to a firm; every other endpoint answers 403 for them, and this is the one place that says so as an answer rather than an error. `undefined` here is the state a client should render as "ask your firm's administrator to add you", never as a failure.

id.description: The firm's id.

name.description: The firm's name, for the header.

firstName.description:
The two halves of this user's name, as their firm recorded them.

**Either may be `''`, and that means "never recorded"** — not "blank". Rows written before the name was two fields carry one display string, and the server derives what it can from it; a name it cannot split yields an empty surname. A client that requires a real name is expected to ask, which is the state these two exist to make visible.

displayName.description:
The composed name, for rendering. **Server-derived — there is nothing to write here.** Send `UpdateMeRequest` with the halves instead.

It stays on the wire because most callers only ever show a name: a screen rendering "opened by" reads this one field and never needs the halves.

isAdmin.description: Full access to every feature, every case, and the firm's user list.

accessAllCases.description: Every case in the firm, without being linked to them one by one. Independent of `isAdmin` on purpose — a supervising attorney can have this without also being able to manage users.

permissions.description: The EFFECTIVE level per feature, not the stored map: an administrator's record says `firm_administration: 'hidden'` and they can nonetheless manage users, so this is what the server will actually allow. Use `permits` rather than comparing strings.

defaultCourt.description: The firm's defaults for a new case and its letterhead (issue #360), on the ONE route every member may read — the create form prefills from them, and a paralegal who cannot read `/v1/firm` still opens cases.

signatureBlock.description: The caller's own standing signature block, or `null` when none is set.

FirmQuestionnaire.description: `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /v1/firm/questionnaire` — EVERY section, switched off or not. `isDefault` means the firm has stored nothing (never saved, or reset); `updatedAt`/`updatedBy` are `null` then.

updatedBy.description: The subject of the firm user who last saved it.

FirmQuestionnaireSection.description: One section as a FIRM USER configures it — `GET /v1/firm/questionnaire`.

covers.description: What the section maps to on the petition and schedules — for staff.

switchable.description: False for `personal_information`, which is always on.

enabled.description: Whether the firm's clients see it. Staff always do.

instructions.description: The firm's own instructions, or `null` when the default is in force.

FirmRole.description: A firm user's job title. Drives server-side DEFAULTS and decides nothing.

FirmStatus.description: Whether the firm may be used at all. Reading `suspended` through this client is nearly hypothetical: accessor resolution refuses every member of a suspended firm, so the routes that return a `Firm` answer 403 before they could say it.

FirmUser.description:
A firm user as `GET /v1/firm/users` returns them — the whole record, for administrators only.

`permissions` here is the STORED map, unlike `FirmMembership`'s: an administrator editing somebody's record needs to see the stored value and the admin override as two separate facts, or turning off `isAdmin` looks like it grants nothing back.

subject.description: The Cognito subject — the id every other endpoint addresses them by.

email.description: Their email address, which is also their sign-in username.

firstName.description: The two halves of their name. Either may be `''` — see `FirmMembership`.

displayName.description: Their composed name, for display. Server-derived.

isAdmin.description: Full access to every feature, every case, and the firm's user list.

accessAllCases.description: Every case in the firm, without per-case linking.

permissions.description: The stored per-feature map — see the note above.

createdAt.description: The server's UTC creation timestamp, verbatim.

updatedAt.description: The server's UTC last-update timestamp, verbatim.

FirmUserStatus.description: Whether a firm user's account is usable.

FormMetric.description:
One hub row's single number — `form_metric_json`'s exact shape.

`value` is always a STRING, for the same reason `CaseTotals`' members are: a `'total'` is a decimal amount, and even a `'count'` is kept a string so the wire type does not change with the kind. Never parse and re-render it — show it as given.

FormMetricKind.description: Whether `FormMetric.value` counts entities or totals a dollar figure.

FormPreview.description:
`GET /v1/cases/{caseId}/forms/{form}/preview` — the creditor-matrix route's own 200-either-way contract, applied to one form: a short-lived download URL (`problems` empty), or every reason it could not render yet (`problems` non-empty, the three URL members absent) — never both, and never a partial form.

`url`/`method`/`expiresAt` are the same bearer capability `PacketDownload` carries; do not log or cache the URL.

options.description: The output options (issue 13.11) this render was requested with — echoed either way, blocked or rendered.

HazardousProperty.description: B101 line 14: property needing immediate attention.

HouseholdFigure.description: A household size the engine read, and where it came from — both `null` until the inputs can answer it.

IncomeLineOverride.description: One entered B122A-1 income line (issue #349), replacing what the dated records derive for that column; `id` is client-chosen and required (provenance). One row per column per line — the server refuses a second.

Job.description:
A pipeline job, as returned by both `/v1/cases/{caseId}/jobs` endpoints: `{"id", "kind", "status", "createdBy", "attempts", "createdAt", "updatedAt"}` plus `failure` only when failed and `result` only when succeeded — both **absent** otherwise, never `null`.

There is no `caseId`: the caller named the case in the URL.

id.description: The server-generated job id — the handle `InsolviaApiClient.getCaseJob` polls.

createdBy.description: The subject of the firm user who accepted the job. Keyed the same way `FirmColleague.subject` is — resolve it through `listFirmDirectory`, never render it raw.

attempts.description: How many times a worker has started this job. 0 until the first run.

documentId.description: Present only on the document-scoped kinds (`document_extraction`).

options.description:
Present only on the options-scoped kinds (`packet_assembly`, issue
13.11) — always the full, canonicalised shape once present, defaults filled in, never the caller's partial request.

result.description: Present only when `status` is `'succeeded'`. Shape is per-kind.

JobFailure.description: Why a job failed, in words safe to show the preparer. `category` is a machine key (`case_incomplete`, `internal`, …); `message` is the sentence to render.

JobKind.description: The job kinds the API accepts today. The exact `KINDS` tuple from `core/jobs.py`: `echo` (the walking skeleton), `packet_assembly` (the Chapter 7 packet, issue #96) and `petition_review` (the AI review's advisory findings, issue #97).

JobStatus.description: Where a job sits. `queued` and `running` mean poll again; `succeeded` and `failed` are settled — except that a `failed` job whose failure was infrastructure (category `internal`) is still being retried by the pipeline and may yet flip to `succeeded`. Only `succeeded` never changes.

Letterhead.description: What the firm prints at the top of a letter and on the signer block's firm lines (issue #360). Snake_case inside, like every case-domain body: the address IS the case domain's `Address`, and the block is copied onto a `FilingProfessionalBody` by key.

LibraryCreditor.description:
A firm's reusable creditor (issue 13.9 / #350) — `/v1/firm/creditors`, gated by the `creditor_library` feature.

**Snake_case, unlike every other type on this page.** Every other firm-domain response (`Firm`, `FirmUser`) is camelCase because `firm.py` invented its own field names; this one reuses `claims.py`'s `NoticeParty` and the case domain's `Address` verbatim (the issue specifies "the same shape `claim.notice_parties` uses"), so the wire follows the case domain's snake_case rather than adding a second, camelCase copy of the same fields.

additional_notice_parties.description: Other parties to notify about a debt to this creditor — copy target for a claim's `ClaimBody.notice_parties` once the claim exists; not copied onto the case creditor itself, which carries no such field.

preferred.description: Surfaced first by a picker; set by whoever curates the library.

LibraryCreditorDraft.description: The `POST` / `PUT /v1/firm/creditors/{id}` request body — a WHOLE record, never a partial PATCH. `insolvia_core.library_creditors` owns why: every field is edited together on one form, and `notes` must be able to become empty again, which "omitted means unchanged" cannot express for the same field that also needs "omitted means clear it".

name.description: Required — a library entry with no name is not a record the picker can show.

LifecycleEvent.description: One event in a case's lifecycle history (ADR 0027), oldest first. The optional members are present only on the kinds they belong to.

effectiveOn.description: The court date the event takes effect, `YYYY-MM-DD`; `null` when it has none.

recordedBy.description: The subject of the person who recorded it.

LiquidationAsset.description: One asset's row of the liquidation analysis.

ListCasesResult.description:
The `GET /v1/cases` 200 response: `{"cases", "nextCursor"?}`.

`nextCursor` is **absent, not `null`**, when there are no more pages — mirroring the wire exactly, the same convention this package's request models use for absent optional fields.

nextCursor.description: An opaque cursor for the next page, or absent on the last page.

LocalStandardsFigures.description: The IRS Local Standards for the case's county (B122A-2 lines 8-14). `null` on any figure means that county is outside the launch states this release covers, or the jurisdiction has not been entered yet — see `CaseStandards.problems` for which.

MaritalAdjustmentItem.description: One B122A-2 line-3 (B122C-1 line-13) row; `id` is client-chosen and required (provenance).

MeansTestChapter13.description: The Chapter 13 verdict (issue #365): B122C-1's applicable commitment period under § 1325(b)(4) with the comparison that set it, whether § 1325(b)(3) requires Form 122C-2 (line 17b), and — when it does — B122C-2 line 45, the monthly disposable income the plan must commit. `null` on a Chapter 7 trace and while the engine has not run.

commitmentMaritalAdjustment.description: B122C-1 line 19a — the adjustment deducted for the commitment period.

MeansTestExemptions.description: The exemptions as entered, and which one (if any) ended the test.

rule.description: The statute and form part granting `applied`.

MeansTestHousehold.description: The three household sizes and the age bands, as the engine read them.

childrenUnder18.description: Dependents under 18, from the dependents collection (line 29's cap).

MeansTestLine.description: One line of the calculation trace: the form it prints on (B122C-1's Part 2-3 lines and B122C-2's lines share numbers, issue #365), the printed line number, its subject, the computed amount, and where it came from — a dataset release, an entered field, a derived input, or line arithmetic.

MedianComparison.description: B122A-1 lines 12-14: annualized CMI against the applicable median.

source.description: Names the Census table and release the median came from.

NationalStandardsFigures.description: The IRS National Standards allowance for the case's household size (B122A-2 lines 6-7), and the per-person out-of-pocket health-care rates — these apply nationwide, so they are never `null` once a release exists.

NewChecklistItem.description: One entry of a checklist save, or one ad-hoc request.

description.description: Omitted from the body when absent.

Note.description: A note as every note endpoint returns it: server identity, the author snapshot captured at write, and whatever of `NoteRequest` is populated. Absent members are absent, never null — the same rule `Debtor` follows.

id.description: The server-generated note id, stable across edits.

author_subject.description: The Cognito subject of whoever wrote this note, captured when it was created and unaffected by later edits — including an admin's, per `putNote`. Never the editor's.

author_name.description: The author's display name, captured at the same moment as `author_subject`.

form_series.description: A form series id, exactly as `CaseForm.series` names it (e.g. `"form/b106g"`) — the form this note is anchored to, or absent for a case-level note.

NoteRequest.description: The client-supplied half of a note: everything but its server identity and its server-stamped author. Used for both create and edit — there is no partial update, the same PUT-replaces-whole rule `PutDebtorRequest` follows.

form_series.description: A form series id, exactly as `CaseForm.series` names it (e.g. `"form/b106g"`) — the form this note is anchored to, or absent for a case-level note.

NoticeParty.description: 106D Part 2 / 106E/F Part 3: someone else to be notified about a debt. `id` is the client-chosen row id, required for the same reason `OtherName.id` is: provenance addresses the row by it.

OtherName.description:
An 8-year-lookback alias.

**`id` is required here even though the API will generate one**, and that is not defensiveness — a generated id makes the request impossible to satisfy. Provenance addresses this row as `other_names_used[<id>].surname`, so a client that omits the id cannot write provenance for the fields it is sending, and the API rejects any populated field with no provenance. The id must therefore be the client's, chosen before the request. It has to match `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`; anything else is refused rather than replaced.

id.description: The client-chosen row id. Matches `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`. See above.

OtherSecuredPayment.description:
One B122A-2 line-33d row; `id` is client-chosen and required (provenance).

Widened by issue #349 so the row can be entered BESIDE the secured claim it belongs to: `claim_id` keys it to that claim, `bucket` says which IRS ownership line its payment offsets, and `cure_total` is the past-due amount line 34 divides by 60. The engine sums the bucketed rows where the single typed totals on the body are absent — never both.

OutputOptions.description: The output options an already-produced `Packet` or `FormPreview` was rendered with — `output_options_json`'s exact shape, every field present so "the plain filing set" is itself a recorded fact, not an absence. `forms` is absent, never an empty array, when every form the case files was included (only `Packet.options` ever carries it — a preview already names its one form).

printDate.description: Today's date and time in the top margin of every page.

signElectronically.description: `/s/ <name>` filled onto each debtor's own signature line (never the attorney's). Combined with `printDate`, the paired date line is also filled with today's date; without it, that date stays wet.

forms.description: The short form keys rendered, when a subset was requested.

amendedOnly.description: Renders an AMENDMENT (issue #370): only the schedules carrying at least one item flagged `amended` (see `CaseEntity`), each printing only its amended items with its own "amended filing" caption ticked, B106Sum/B106Dec re-rendered alongside them, and a generated amendment cover sheet — never an official court form. It is also the one option that lets a FILED case's packet assembly run at all.

OutputOptionsRequest.description: The request-side shape: every field optional and, per this package's omit-when-absent rule, left out of the wire body/query entirely rather than sent as `false`/`"all"` — the server fills in exactly the same defaults `OutputOptions` states explicitly once rendered.

forms.description: Packet assembly only — `InsolviaApiClient.getCaseFormPreview` already names one form.

amendedOnly.description: See `OutputOptions.amendedOnly`. Refused server-side when combined with `forms`.

Packet.description:
One assembled Chapter 7 packet, as returned by `GET /v1/cases/{caseId}/packets`. Produced by the `packet_assembly` pipeline job — trigger with `InsolviaApiClient.acceptCaseJob`, poll with `InsolviaApiClient.getCaseJob`, then download through `InsolviaApiClient.getPacketUrl`.

A packet is immutable: re-assembly creates a NEW record rather than replacing this one, so the packet an attorney reviewed stays the packet they reviewed.

id.description: The server-generated packet id.

caseId.description: The case it belongs to (also named in the URL; echoed for convenience).

jobId.description: The pipeline job whose run produced it.

fileName.description: The download name — the case's chapter: `chapter7-packet.zip` or `chapter13-packet.zip`.

byteSize.description: The stored zip's exact size in bytes.

sha256.description: The sha256 of the stored zip. Assembly is deterministic to the byte, so this digest is how a reviewer proves a downloaded file is THIS packet.

formRevisions.description: The effective-dating pins this packet was rendered under — the same map written onto the case, kept here because the case's copy moves on re-assembly while this record describes this packet forever.

constantsSetId.description: The `code/dollar-amounts` release this packet was rendered under — the second pin, kept here for `formRevisions`' reason.

creditorCount.description: How many creditors the enclosed matrix lists (after deduplication).

createdBy.description: The subject of the firm user whose job accept produced it — resolve through `listFirmDirectory`, never render raw.

options.description: The output options (issue 13.11) this packet was rendered with — a plain `{draftWatermark: false, printDate: false, signaturePages: 'all', signElectronically: false}` for the ordinary filing set. What tells a draft apart from a filing set after the fact.

PayPeriodDeduction.description: One itemised deduction line on a stub. `id` is caller-chosen and required — the same contract as a claim's notice parties, so provenance can address `deductions[<id>].amount` across reorders.

description.description: The stub's own wording for the line.

PermissionLevel.description: How much of a feature a firm user may reach. Ordered weakest to strongest: `add_edit` satisfies anything `view_only` does.

PersonName.description: A debtor's legal name. Every part is optional — intake is progressive.

suffix.description: Max 20 characters, where the other parts allow 200.

PlanBestInterests.description: The best-interests comparison; `passes` is `null` while undetermined.

PlanClass.description: One class of the waterfall: its totals, its months, and its rows.

PlanCommitmentPeriod.description: The commitment period the means test set, and why.

PlanFeasibility.description: Whether the payments over the term cover the waterfall. `feasible` is `null` while an input the waterfall needs is missing.

PlanFunding.description: What goes into the plan, month by month.

PlanLiquidation.description: The § 1325(a)(4) hypothetical Chapter 7: property less liens, exemptions, the § 326(a) commission, other costs and priority claims — `available` to general unsecured creditors, as `percentage` of the Chapter 7 pool.

PlanLumpSum.description: A one-time payment into the plan in `month`.

PlanPayoutRow.description: One payee's line of the waterfall — a claim, the trustee, the attorney. `allowed` is what the plan owes it before interest; `principal` and `interest` what the term pays; months are 1-based and `null` when nothing was paid. `source` names the claim, the plan field or the rule behind it.

PlanPoolClaim.description: One claim's part of an unsecured pool, and why it is there.

PlanReceivedLumpSum.description: One lump sum the plan receives.

PlanScenario.description: One calculated alternative, in the order sent.

PlanSecuredTreatment.description: How the plan treats one secured claim. `arrearage`, `arrearage_interest_rate` and `maintenance_payment` (a conduit payment, absent = paid directly) belong to a cure; `cramdown_value` (absent = the derived secured portion) and `interest_rate` to a cramdown; `monthly_payment` fixes the equal monthly payment for either (absent = amortised over the term). `id` is client-chosen and required.

PlanStepPayment.description: From `start_month` on (1-based), the monthly payment is `monthly_payment`.

PlanUnsecured.description: The plan's general unsecured class: who is in it and what it is owed.

PortalAnswer.description: A client's own answer, as `/v1/portal/answers` returns it — the value they gave and where it stands. An answer is a candidate in the firm's review queue: `pending` until a person at the firm accepts (`accepted` / `corrected`) or rejects it, or the client withdraws it. Only `pending` may be changed or withdrawn.

PortalAnswerValue.description: An answer's value: input key → that input's value.

PortalCaseStatus.description: What a client may read of their case (ADR 0023 decision 4): its chapter and its stage. `stage` is the case's lifecycle status, read server-side through a projection that takes the client's binding.

PortalClient.description: A client bound to a case, as a FIRM USER sees them.

subject.description: The client's Cognito subject — the key the resend and revoke calls take.

displayName.description: The name the firm gave at invitation — what the review queue shows.

invitedBy.description: The subject of the firm user who invited them.

PortalClientStatus.description: `invited` until the client's first portal request, `active` after it, `revoked` once the firm withdraws access (kept, not deleted).

PortalDocumentRequest.description: One request as the CLIENT reads it, with their own uploads against it.

PortalMe.description: `GET /v1/portal/me` — who the portal says the signed-in CLIENT is. Called with a portal session's token, never a staff one. Deliberately carries no case id: no portal URL names a case.

case.description: The bound case's public status — and nothing else of the case record.

PortalQuestion.description: One question as the portal renders it (`insolvia_core.questions`). Where the answer lands in the case is the server's business and is not sent. `repeats`: many answers (each vehicle), else one live answer at a time — a second while the first is pending is a 409; change the first instead. `perDebtor`: answered for a filing role.

PortalQuestionInput.description: One box of a question. `key` is the key in the answer's `value`.

PortalQuestionnaireSection.description: One section as the CLIENT reads it — title, the instructions in force, and (ADR 0023 PR 4) its questions in order.

PortalUpload.description: A CLIENT's own upload, as the portal shows it — no case id.

Principal.description:
The `GET /v1/me` 200 response: the signed-in caller's identity, derived purely from claims the access token already proved. The API makes no call to Cognito to build it.

**The body is camelCase, like every other endpoint** — `{"subject", "username", "clientId", "scopes", "expiresAt"}`, matching `submittedAt` on the waitlist route. The underlying JWT claims are snake_case (`client_id`, `exp`), and the API translates at its edge rather than leaking claim spelling into its own wire format. Models here mirror that wire exactly and never translate again, so this file shows what actually goes over the socket.

**There is no email.** The Cognito pool sets `username_attributes = ["email"]`, so an access token's `username` claim is a pool-generated UUID and no address appears in any access-token claim. Treat `username` as an opaque correlation id — never render it as an email address. The app displays the address from the ID token it holds.

subject.description: The `sub` claim: the pool's stable, immutable user id. The only value that should ever key user-owned data.

username.description: Cognito's `username` claim — a generated UUID, **not** an email address. `null` when the token carried no username.

clientId.description: The Cognito app client the token was minted for.

scopes.description: OAuth scopes on the token. Nothing enforces them server-side today.

expiresAt.description: The token's `exp` as a Unix timestamp in **seconds** (not milliseconds — it is the JWT claim verbatim), or `null` when absent.

firm.description: The caller's firm and standing in it, or **absent** when nobody has added them to one. See `FirmMembership` — `undefined` here is what a client should render as "ask your firm's administrator to add you", and it is the only endpoint that reports that state rather than refusing.

ProvenanceEntry.description:
Where one field's value came from.

**`confirmed_by` and `confirmed_at` are one act, not two fields** — a human said "yes, that is right" at a moment — and the API enforces that: a `ai_extracted` or `imported` entry with either half missing is rejected with a 400, because "nothing extracted enters the case until a human confirms it" is a property of the store rather than a promise about the UI. A `staff_typed` entry needs neither: the person typing it *is* the confirmation.

Every member but `source` is omitted from the wire when absent, in both directions — see `putDebtorRequestToJson`.

confirmed_by.description: The person who confirmed it. Required when `source` is machine-supplied.

confirmed_at.description: When it was confirmed, as a UTC ISO-8601 `Z` string. Required when `source` is machine-supplied, and the API parses it — a string of the right shape that is not a real instant is refused.

document_id.description: The document the value was read from.

locator.description: Where in that document — an opaque map the API stores but does not interpret.

extraction_id.description: The extraction run that produced the value.

confidence.description: The extractor's confidence, between 0 and 1 inclusive.

library_creditor_id.description: The `LibraryCreditor.id` this value was copied from. Present only when `source` is `'library'`. Not validated against the firm's library by the API — a library entry deleted after the copy leaves this readable rather than the case record unwritable.

client_id.description: The `FirmClient.id` this value was copied from. Present only when `source` is `'client'`. Not validated against the directory — an archived or merged client leaves the provenance readable.

copied_from_case_id.description: The case this value was COPIED from (`POST /v1/cases/{id}/copy`, issue #355) — alongside, not instead of, the value's own `source`: a confirmed extraction copied forward is still that, and `document_id` still names the source case's document. A client must echo it back unchanged on a save that did not touch the value, which `provenanceToJson` does.

PutDebtorRequest.description:
The `PUT /v1/cases/{caseId}/debtors/{filingRole}` request body: a `DebtorBody` plus its `provenance`.

**Whole, not partial.** The endpoint is a PUT and replaces the record, so anything left out is gone rather than left alone. That is a consequence of the provenance rule rather than a preference: "every populated field carries provenance" can only be checked against a complete record, and a partial write would have to merge against the stored copy and re-derive the rule afterwards. The questionnaire holds the whole record client-side anyway, so autosave sends it.

**`tax_id` follows the same rule with one wrinkle.** The record is whole, but the client never holds the whole number after a save — only its last four — so a save that did not touch it echoes the `TaxIdView` it was given and the API keeps the stored number (`TaxIdEntry`). Leaving it out clears it, exactly as for any other field.

provenance.description: Where each populated field came from. Omitted when empty, which is what an entirely blank record sends. Build it with `staffTypedProvenance` rather than by hand.

other_names_used.description: Aliases used in the last 8 years. Each row needs a client-chosen `OtherName.id`.

employer_ids.description: Employer identification numbers. Each max 20 characters.

signed_at.description: The signature date, `YYYY-MM-DD` — a calendar fact, not an instant, so no time and no zone (see docs/reference/case-data-model.md). The API parses it as a real date and rejects anything else, including a timestamp and the compact `20260805` form. `DateInput` in `@insolvia-ai/design-system` emits exactly this.

tax_id.description: The SSN or ITIN (issue 13.12 / #382): a `TaxIdEntry` on the way in, a `TaxIdView` on the way out (`Debtor` narrows it). Its provenance is ONE entry at the path `tax_id` — the kind and the digits are one identifier entered in one act — which `staffTypedProvenance` handles as the one exception to its walk.

ReviewAction.description: What a reviewer may do with one pending candidate.

ReviewCandidateRequest.description: The review request: `accept` (optionally with the record as the human corrected it — full body, same shape as the collection's own PUT) or `reject`. One candidate per call, deliberately: bulk-accept must not become blind-accept.

ReviewedCandidate.description: A review's answer: the resolved candidate, plus the record an accept wrote.

record.description: Present exactly when the action was an accept.

SignatureBlock.description: An attorney's standing signature block (issue #360) — exactly the `FilingProfessionalBody` keys that do not change from case to case, so the petition screen's "use firm default" spreads it onto the record without a mapping. The name is not here: it is the firm user's own.

SignaturePagesMode.description: Which pages of a rendered form to keep: every page (`'all'`), only the pages carrying a signature line (`'only'` — a signing-meeting print), or every page EXCEPT those (`'omit'`). A form with no signature line of its own contributes nothing under `'only'`; a form that is entirely a signature block (B106Dec) contributes nothing under `'omit'`.

SourcedAmount.description: A figure and where it came from.

SpecialCircumstanceItem.description: One B122C-2 line-43 row (issue #365): a special circumstance that justifies an additional expense (§ 707(b)(2)(B)), which on the Chapter 13 form is a deduction in the arithmetic. `id` is client-chosen and required.

StatutoryLimitFigure.description: A federal § 522 cap in force on the resolution date — not itself claimable.

Task.description:
One task of a case, as every task endpoint returns it.

`overdue` is server-COMPUTED on every read, never stored — it is `true` only when `dueDate` is in the past AND `done` is `false`. Do not compute your own version from `dueDate`; the server's clock and "today" are the ones that count, and computing it independently invites the client and the server disagreeing right at a day boundary.

assigneeSubject.description: The assignee's Cognito subject — resolve it through the firm directory, same as `CaseAssignee.subject`. Absent means unassigned.

formSeries.description: The short form key this task anchors to (`"b106d"`, not `"form/b106d"`) — the same spelling `CaseForm.form` carries. Absent means no anchor.

completedAt.description: Present only once `done` has been `true`; absent on a task never completed or since reopened.

createdBy.description: The subject of whoever added it — an audit fact, like `Case.createdBy`. Grants nothing on its own.

TaxIdEntry.description:
The tax identifier as a write carries it — ONE of two shapes:

- `{ kind, value }`: a number being entered, nine digits with or without   dashes. The API validates the shape (SSN vs ITIN rules) and seals it.
- `{ kind, last_four }`: the `TaxIdView` a read returned, echoed   back to mean "keep what is stored". A PUT replaces the whole record   (`PutDebtorRequest`) and a client only ever holds the last four,   so this is how a save that did not touch the number carries it across.   The API refuses an echo that does not match what it holds.

Both members present is refused; neither present is refused. Leaving `tax_id` off the request altogether clears the stored number. A client that holds both — a number on file and one being typed — sends the typed one; `putDebtorRequestToJson` applies that rule.

TaxIdView.description: The tax identifier as EVERY read returns it: the kind and the last four digits, nothing more. The full number is stored encrypted and has no wire shape at all — no endpoint returns it, and the MCP tools cannot either (docs/reference/mcp-surface.md). The one form that prints it, B121, reads it server-side through an audited read.

UnsecuredSource.description: Whether a claim's unsecured portion was derived or typed by a preparer.

UpdateCaseBody.description: `PATCH /v1/cases/{caseId}` as sent: any subset, each key absent to leave it unchanged and `null` (where allowed) to clear it. The client's `UpdateCaseChanges` nests the court and camel-cases the rest.

UpdateFirmRequest.description:
The `PATCH /v1/firm` request body — the name, the defaults and the letterhead (issue #360), each optional; an empty body is a 400.

`defaultCourt` and `defaultDivision` are read as a PAIR by the server: send both codes to set, both `null` to clear. `null` on any default clears it; omitted leaves it alone.

**`status` is absent on purpose and never joins.** Suspend/reactivate is Insolvia's own operation, on the admin portal: a firm suspending itself would be a lockout with no self-service recovery, because self-signup is off and a suspended firm's members — the caller included — are refused everywhere.

UpdateFirmUserRequest.description:
The `PATCH /v1/firm/users/{subject}` request body. Every field optional; an empty body is a 400 rather than a no-op.

**`permissions` REPLACES the stored map**, unlike `AddFirmUserRequest`'s. A merging PATCH could only ever grant — there would be no way to express "take documents away" — so send the map you want.

**`email` is absent on purpose.** The address is the one Cognito authenticates and sends to; changing it in our store alone would leave two systems disagreeing about who somebody is.

signatureBlock.description: A colleague's signature block (issue #360); `null` clears it.

UpdateMeRequest.description:
The `PATCH /v1/me` request body — your own name, and nothing else.

Two optional fields where `UpdateFirmUserRequest` has six, and the narrowness is the contract: everything else on the record is an administrator's statement about you (role, permissions, status — sent through `InsolviaApiClient.updateFirmUser`), and email is a pool fact neither endpoint accepts.

**Both halves are optional, but the server refuses a body with neither.** Either alone is a legitimate edit: a row whose halves were derived from a pre-split display name often has a correct first name and an empty surname, and making that person retype both would be rude.

`displayName` is deliberately absent — it is derived on the way out, so there is nothing here to write it with.

signatureBlock.description: Your own signature block (issue #360) — a bar number is the attorney's own fact, so it is self-service like the name. `null` clears it; omitted leaves it alone.

UpdateTaskRequest.description:
The `PATCH /v1/cases/{caseId}/tasks/{taskId}` request body — edit, reassign, complete or reopen a task, all through this one shape.

**THREE STATES, not two, for `description`, `dueDate`, `assigneeSubject` and `formSeries`.** Leave the key OUT of the object entirely to leave that field unchanged; set it to `null` to CLEAR it (unassign a task, remove a due date); set it to a value to replace it. `updateTaskRequestToJson` reads which keys are actually present with the `in` operator, so build the object literally — `{ dueDate: null }`, never `{ dueDate: undefined }`, which is indistinguishable from omitting the key at the JSON layer and would be silently read as "leave unchanged" by the wire format, not "clear".

`subject` cannot be cleared, only replaced — a task with no title is not a task. `done` follows the same two-state rule `subject` does: set it to complete or reopen the task, and `Task.completedAt` follows it server-side — never send `completedAt` yourself, there is nowhere to send it.

explanation.description: The explanation the form asks for when `basis` is `other`. Max 1000.

WaitlistSubmission.description:
The `POST /v1/waitlist` request body.

`name`, `firm`, and `email` are required by the API; the rest are optional and omitted from the JSON entirely when absent (the API treats absent and empty identically, but omitting keeps requests minimal and mirrors what the marketing form sends).

The optional fields are typed `string | undefined` rather than leaning on `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` to forbid an explicit `undefined`: a form hands you `string | undefined` values, and making every call site build the object conditionally would scatter the omit-when-absent rule across the codebase. The rule lives in exactly one place instead — `waitlistSubmissionToJson`, which treats absent and `undefined` identically and never emits `null` or `""`.

name.description: The submitter's name. Required; max 200 characters.

firm.description: The submitter's firm. Required; max 200 characters.

email.description: A work email address. Required; max 320 characters.

currentSoftware.description: The bankruptcy software the firm uses today. Optional; max 100.

message.description: A free-text message. Optional; max 2000 characters.

host.description: The serving host the submission came from (set server-to-server by the marketing SSR action, not visitor input). Optional; max 253.

Error.description: A refusal, in the shared error envelope.

fields.description: Per-field messages, on a 400 that names fields.

staff.description: A firm user's Cognito access token, minted for the app's client. A portal token is refused.

client.description: A debtor's Cognito access token, minted for the client portal's app client (ADR 0023). It reaches only `/v1/portal/` routes.

calendarToken.name: token
calendarToken.description: A calendar feed token from `POST /v1/me/calendar-token`, for calendar apps that cannot send a header.
